description: Available question set on landforms created by different agents for FDA/SDA practice. Coverage has not been verified against the complete source material; check and expand it before formal use.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a landform?

options.A: A natural physical feature of the Earth's surface
options.B: A man-made structure on the Earth's surface
options.C: A type of rock formation only

questions.explanation: A landform is a natural physical feature of the Earth's surface, such as a valley, mountain, plain, dune, cliff or delta.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Landforms develop through the interaction of which two types of processes?
questions.explanation: Landforms develop through the interaction of internal (endogenic) and external (exogenic) processes.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What are geomorphic agents?

options.A: Natural media or forces that erode, transport and deposit material

questions.explanation: Geomorphic agents are natural media or forces that erode, transport and deposit material, thereby shaping the Earth's surface. Major agents include running water, glaciers, wind, sea waves and groundwater.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a major geomorphic agent mentioned in the text?
questions.explanation: Major agents include running water, glaciers, wind, sea waves and groundwater. Volcanic eruptions are endogenic processes, not listed as a geomorphic agent in this context.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: How are landforms classified by their dominant agent?

options.A: Fluvial, glacial, aeolian, coastal/marine and karst

questions.explanation: Landforms are classified as fluvial (river), glacial, aeolian (wind), coastal/marine and karst (groundwater solution) landforms.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is meant by a polygenetic landform?

options.A: A landform formed by more than one process
options.B: A landform formed by only one process
options.C: A landform formed only by wind
options.D: A landform formed only by water

questions.explanation: Some landforms are polygenetic, meaning that more than one process contributed to their development.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is the difference between erosional and depositional landforms?

options.A: Erosional landforms are carved by removal of material; depositional landforms are built by accumulation of sediment
options.B: Erosional landforms are built by accumulation; depositional landforms are carved by removal
options.C: Both are formed only by wind
options.D: Both are formed only by glaciers

questions.explanation: Erosional landforms are carved or produced mainly by removal of material; depositional landforms are built by accumulation of transported sediment. Some features involve both processes at different stages.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What are fluvial landforms?

options.A: Landforms produced by running water in rivers and streams

questions.explanation: Fluvial landforms are landforms produced by running water in rivers and streams through erosion, transportation and deposition.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The dominant process in a river changes with which of the following factors?

options.A: Gradient, discharge, sediment load, channel form and geology

questions.explanation: The dominant process changes with gradient, discharge, sediment load, channel form and geology.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The upper course of a river commonly has:

options.A: A steep gradient and strong vertical erosion
options.B: A gentle gradient and extensive deposition

questions.explanation: The upper course commonly has a steep gradient and strong vertical erosion.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The middle course of a river often shows:
questions.explanation: The middle course often shows greater lateral erosion and meandering.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The lower course of a river commonly has:

options.A: A gentler gradient and extensive deposition
options.B: A steep gradient and strong vertical erosion

questions.explanation: The lower course commonly has a gentler gradient and extensive deposition.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: How is a V-shaped valley formed?

options.A: A river cuts downwards into its bed while weathering and mass movement weaken the valley sides
options.B: A glacier widens and deepens a valley

questions.explanation: A river cuts downwards into its bed, while weathering and mass movement weaken the valley sides. Material moves downslope and is carried away, leaving a narrow valley with steep sides and a V-shaped cross-section.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What are interlocking spurs?

options.A: Projecting ridges of resistant land that alternate from side to side in the upper course of a river
options.B: Depositional features on the inner bank of a meander

questions.explanation: Interlocking spurs are projecting ridges of resistant land that alternate from side to side in the upper course of a river. A young river follows the path of least resistance around them rather than cutting straight through.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: How does a waterfall form?

options.A: Where resistant rock overlies or adjoins less resistant rock, softer rock erodes more rapidly forming a step
options.B: Where a river enters a standing body of water

questions.explanation: A waterfall commonly develops where resistant rock overlies or adjoins less resistant rock. Softer rock is eroded more rapidly, forming a step. Hydraulic action and abrasion deepen a plunge pool and undercut the hard-rock ledge; collapse and retreat may leave a gorge.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a plunge pool?

options.A: A deep basin at the foot of a waterfall formed by the force of falling water and abrasion
options.B: A shallow lake on a floodplain

questions.explanation: A plunge pool is a deep basin at the foot of a waterfall formed by the force of falling water and the abrasion of rock fragments carried in the turbulent water.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a gorge?
questions.explanation: A gorge is a narrow, steep-sided valley. It may form through river incision or through the upstream retreat of a waterfall as undercut rock collapses.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a meander?

options.A: A winding bend or loop in a river channel
options.B: A straight section of a river

questions.explanation: A meander is a winding bend or loop in a river channel. Faster flow and greater erosion commonly occur near the outer bank (cut bank), while slower flow and deposition occur near the inner bank (point bar).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Why does a river meander?

options.A: Small irregularities in the channel produce variations in velocity and pressure, promoting erosion on the outer bank and deposition on the inner bank

questions.explanation: Small irregularities in the channel produce variations in velocity and pressure. Helicoidal flow and the concentration of faster flow near the outer bank promote erosion there, while sediment accumulates on the inner bank. The bend can enlarge and migrate.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a cut bank?

options.A: The eroding outer bank of a meander
options.B: The depositional inner bank of a meander
options.C: A ridge of sand deposited by longshore drift

questions.explanation: A cut bank is the eroding outer bank of a meander.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a point bar?

options.A: A depositional feature on the inner bank of a meander where sand and gravel accumulate
options.B: The eroding outer bank of a meander

questions.explanation: A point bar is a depositional feature on the inner bank of a meander where sand and gravel accumulate.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: How does an ox-bow lake form?

options.A: Continued lateral erosion narrows the neck of a meander; during a flood, the river cuts through the narrow neck, abandoning the old loop
options.B: A glacier melts and leaves a hollow

questions.explanation: Continued lateral erosion narrows the neck of a meander. During a flood, the river may cut through the narrow neck and adopt a straighter course. Deposition seals the ends of the abandoned loop, leaving a crescent-shaped ox-bow lake.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a floodplain?

options.A: A broad, relatively flat area beside a river built by repeated overbank deposition during floods
options.D: A hill formed by glacial deposition

questions.explanation: A floodplain is a broad, relatively flat area beside a river built by repeated overbank deposition during floods, together with channel migration and associated sedimentation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a natural levee?

options.A: A low ridge of sediment along a river bank built by overbank flood deposition

questions.explanation: A natural levee is a low ridge of sediment along a river bank. During floods, water spills out of the channel, loses velocity and deposits relatively coarse material near the banks, building raised margins.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is an alluvial fan?

options.A: A fan- or cone-shaped deposit of alluvium formed where a stream emerges from a steep mountain valley onto a flatter plain
options.B: A deposit at a river mouth in the sea

questions.explanation: An alluvial fan is a fan- or cone-shaped deposit of alluvium formed where a stream emerges from a steep mountain valley onto a flatter plain, loses velocity and spreads across a wider area. Coarser material is often deposited near the apex.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: How does an alluvial fan differ from a delta?

options.A: An alluvial fan forms where a stream leaves a steep confined valley for a flatter plain; a delta forms where a river enters a standing body of water
options.B: An alluvial fan forms at a river mouth; a delta forms at a mountain front
options.C: An alluvial fan is glacial; a delta is aeolian

questions.explanation: An alluvial fan forms where a stream leaves a steep confined valley for a flatter plain; a delta forms where a river enters a standing body of water and deposits sediment at its mouth.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a delta?

options.A: A depositional landform at a river mouth where sediment accumulates as the river enters a standing body of water
options.B: A fan-shaped deposit at a mountain front

questions.explanation: A delta is a depositional landform at a river mouth where sediment accumulates as the river enters a sea, lake or other standing water and loses velocity. Its shape depends on river sediment supply, waves, tides and currents.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following are common descriptive forms of deltas?
questions.explanation: Common descriptive forms include arcuate (fan-shaped), bird-foot or digitate, and cuspate deltas.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Process-based classifications of deltas distinguish which types?
questions.explanation: Process-based classifications distinguish river-dominated, wave-dominated and tide-dominated deltas.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a distributary?

options.A: A channel that branches away from the main river and carries water and sediment across a delta
options.B: A tributary that joins the main river

questions.explanation: A distributary is a channel that branches away from the main river and carries water and sediment across a delta towards the sea or lake.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is an important example of river landforms in India?
questions.explanation: Important examples of river landforms in India include the Ganga–Brahmaputra delta and Sundarbans; the Indo-Gangetic floodplain; alluvial fans along Himalayan foothills; meanders and ox-bow lakes in parts of the Ganga and Brahmaputra plains; and deeply incised valleys in Himalayan rivers.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Where in India are meanders and ox-bow lakes commonly found?

options.A: In parts of the Ganga and Brahmaputra plains

questions.explanation: Meanders and ox-bow lakes occur in parts of the Ganga and Brahmaputra plains.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Deeply incised valleys in Himalayan rivers are examples of which type of landform?
questions.explanation: Deeply incised valleys in Himalayan rivers are given as examples of river (fluvial) landforms in India.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What are glacial landforms?

options.A: Landforms created by moving glacier ice and associated meltwater through erosion, transportation and deposition

questions.explanation: Glacial landforms are landforms created by moving glacier ice and associated meltwater through erosion, transportation and deposition.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a cirque, corrie or cwm?

options.A: A steep-sided, armchair-shaped hollow at the head of a glacial valley
options.B: A sharp ridge between two cirques
options.D: A long winding ridge of sand and gravel

questions.explanation: A cirque, corrie or cwm is a steep-sided, armchair-shaped hollow at the head of a glacial valley. Plucking, abrasion, freeze–thaw weathering and nivation may enlarge it; a tarn may occupy the hollow after the ice melts.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a tarn?

options.A: A small mountain lake occupying a cirque or corrie after glacier retreat

questions.explanation: A tarn is a small mountain lake occupying a cirque or corrie after glacier retreat.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What are moraines?

options.A: Ridges or accumulations of debris transported and deposited by glacier ice
options.B: Ridges of sand and gravel deposited by meltwater

questions.explanation: Moraines are ridges or accumulations of debris transported and deposited by glacier ice. They consist of till and may contain a wide range of particle sizes, from clay to boulders.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a lateral moraine?

options.A: A ridge of glacial debris deposited along the side of a valley glacier
options.B: A ridge of debris near the middle of a glacier
options.C: A ridge deposited at the farthest advance of a glacier
options.D: A widespread layer of till beneath the glacier

questions.explanation: A lateral moraine is a ridge of glacial debris deposited along the side of a valley glacier.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a medial moraine?

options.A: A debris ridge near the middle of a glacier, commonly formed when the lateral moraines of two tributary glaciers join
options.B: A ridge deposited along the side of a valley glacier
options.C: A ridge deposited at the farthest advance of a glacier

questions.explanation: A medial moraine is a debris ridge near the middle of a glacier, commonly formed when the lateral moraines of two tributary glaciers join.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a terminal or end moraine?

options.A: A ridge of debris deposited at the farthest advance of a glacier, marking its maximum extent
options.B: A ridge deposited during a temporary pause or minor readvance while a glacier is retreating
options.C: A ridge along the side of a glacier
options.D: A ridge near the middle of a glacier

questions.explanation: A terminal or end moraine is a ridge of debris deposited at the farthest advance of a glacier, marking its maximum extent during that advance.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a ground moraine?

options.A: A widespread layer of till deposited beneath or left behind by glacier ice, often forming gently undulating terrain
options.B: A ridge deposited at the farthest advance of a glacier
options.C: A ridge along the side of a glacier
options.D: A long winding ridge of sand and gravel

questions.explanation: A ground moraine is a widespread layer of till deposited beneath or left behind by glacier ice, often forming gently undulating terrain.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a drumlin?

options.A: An elongated, streamlined hill composed mainly of glacial sediment, commonly aligned with former ice flow
options.B: A long winding ridge of stratified sand and gravel

questions.explanation: A drumlin is an elongated, streamlined hill composed mainly of glacial sediment, commonly aligned with former ice flow. Its precise formation mechanisms are complex and may involve subglacial deposition and deformation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is an esker?

options.A: A long, winding ridge of stratified sand and gravel deposited by meltwater streams flowing within or beneath a glacier
options.B: An elongated streamlined hill of glacial sediment
options.C: A sharp ridge between adjacent cirques

questions.explanation: An esker is a long, winding ridge of stratified sand and gravel deposited by meltwater streams flowing within or beneath a glacier. It remains as a ridge after the ice melts.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a U-shaped valley or glacial trough?

options.A: A broad valley with steep sides and a relatively flat floor, formed when a glacier widens, deepens and straightens a pre-existing river valley
options.B: A narrow valley with steep sides and a V-shaped cross-section formed by river downcutting
options.C: A deep narrow sea inlet flooded by seawater
options.D: A sharp ridge between adjacent cirques

questions.explanation: A U-shaped valley or glacial trough is a broad valley with steep sides and a relatively flat floor, formed when a glacier widens, deepens and straightens a pre-existing river valley.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: How does a U-shaped valley differ from a V-shaped valley?

options.A: A V-shaped valley is commonly produced by river downcutting and slope processes; a U-shaped valley is produced mainly by glacial erosion and has a broader floor and steep sides
options.B: A V-shaped valley is produced by glaciers; a U-shaped valley by rivers
options.C: Both are produced by wind erosion
options.D: Both are produced by groundwater solution

questions.explanation: A V-shaped valley is commonly produced by river downcutting and slope processes; a U-shaped valley is produced mainly by glacial erosion and has a broader floor and steep sides.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is an arete?

options.A: A sharp ridge between adjacent cirques or glacial valleys
options.B: A sharp pyramidal peak formed when several cirques erode back towards one another
options.C: A tributary glacial valley left at a higher elevation than the main trough
options.D: A deep, narrow, steep-sided glacial valley flooded by seawater

questions.explanation: An arete is a sharp ridge between adjacent cirques or glacial valleys.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a horn?

options.A: A sharp pyramidal peak formed when several cirques erode back towards one another
options.B: A sharp ridge between adjacent cirques
options.C: A tributary glacial valley left at a higher elevation
options.D: A long winding ridge of sand and gravel

questions.explanation: A horn is a sharp pyramidal peak formed when several cirques erode back towards one another.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a hanging valley?

options.A: A tributary glacial valley left at a higher elevation than the main glacial trough because the main glacier eroded more deeply
options.B: A U-shaped valley with a broad floor
options.C: A deep narrow sea inlet flooded by seawater
options.D: A sharp ridge between two cirques

questions.explanation: A hanging valley is a tributary glacial valley left at a higher elevation than the main glacial trough because the main glacier eroded more deeply. Waterfalls may occur at its outlet.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a landform?

options.A: A natural physical feature of the Earth's surface
options.B: An artificial structure constructed by humans
options.D: A type of mineral found underground

questions.explanation: A landform is a natural physical feature of the Earth's surface, such as a valley, mountain, plain, dune, cliff or delta.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Landforms develop through the interaction of which two broad categories of processes?
questions.explanation: Landforms develop through the interaction of internal or endogenic processes and external or exogenic processes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are geomorphic agents?

options.A: Natural forces that only increase Earth's temperature
options.B: Natural media or forces that erode, transport and deposit materials
options.D: Internal forces that only produce earthquakes

questions.explanation: Geomorphic agents are natural media or forces responsible for erosion, transportation and deposition, thereby shaping the Earth's surface.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT identified as a major geomorphic agent in the study material?
questions.explanation: The major geomorphic agents include running water, glaciers, wind, sea waves and groundwater.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which term refers to landforms produced by running water?
questions.explanation: Fluvial landforms are produced by rivers and streams through erosion, transportation and deposition.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches the geomorphic agent with its landform classification?
questions.explanation: Aeolian landforms are produced by wind. Fluvial, glacial, coastal and karst landforms are associated with rivers, glaciers, marine processes and groundwater solution respectively.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are polygenetic landforms?

options.C: Landforms produced by volcanic activity alone
options.D: Landforms whose development involves more than one process

questions.explanation: Polygenetic landforms are features whose development has been influenced by more than one geomorphic process.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: An erosional landform is primarily produced by:
questions.explanation: Erosional landforms are mainly produced through the removal of material, whereas depositional landforms develop through sediment accumulation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about erosional and depositional landforms is correct?

options.C: Some landforms involve both erosion and deposition at different stages
options.D: Erosion and deposition cannot occur in the same geographical region

questions.explanation: Some landforms involve erosion during one stage and deposition during another stage of their development.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Fluvial landforms are primarily created by:
questions.explanation: Fluvial landforms are created by rivers and streams through erosion, transportation and deposition.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which combination influences the dominant geomorphic process in a river?

options.A: Latitude, longitude and population density only
options.B: Vegetation colour and atmospheric pressure only
options.C: Gradient, discharge, sediment load, channel form and geology
options.D: Ocean salinity and wind direction only

questions.explanation: The dominant river process changes according to gradient, discharge, sediment load, channel form and underlying geology.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which process is generally dominant in the upper course of a river?
questions.explanation: The upper course commonly has a steep gradient and strong vertical erosion, resulting in deep river incision.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which process commonly becomes more significant in the middle course of a river?
questions.explanation: The middle course commonly shows greater lateral erosion and meandering compared with the upper course.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which process is generally extensive in the lower course of a river?
questions.explanation: The lower course generally has a gentler gradient and extensive deposition of transported sediments.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the upper, middle and lower courses of a river?

options.A: They have rigid boundaries and identical processes in every river
options.B: The upper course is depositional in every geographical setting
options.C: The lower course always has the steepest gradient
options.D: They represent general patterns rather than rigid boundaries

questions.explanation: The upper, middle and lower course model describes general changes in river processes, but the boundaries are not rigid.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A V-shaped valley is primarily associated with:
questions.explanation: A river cuts vertically into its bed while weathering and mass movement weaken the valley sides, producing a V-shaped cross-section.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which processes work together in the formation of a typical V-shaped valley?

options.B: Vertical river erosion, weathering and mass movement

questions.explanation: Vertical river incision combines with weathering and mass movement on valley sides. The loosened material is carried away by the river.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Interlocking spurs are commonly associated with which part of a river?
questions.explanation: Interlocking spurs are projecting ridges that alternate from side to side in the upper course of a river.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why does a young river follow a winding path around interlocking spurs?

options.A: It follows the path of least resistance around projecting ridges
options.B: It is forced to follow ocean currents
options.C: It flows only through limestone caves
options.D: It avoids all areas of lower elevation

questions.explanation: A young river follows the path of least resistance around projecting ridges of resistant land rather than cutting straight through them.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A waterfall commonly develops due to:

options.A: Uniform erosion of rocks of identical resistance
options.B: Differential erosion of resistant and less resistant rocks
options.C: Wind deposition at a river mouth

questions.explanation: A waterfall commonly forms where resistant rock overlies or adjoins less resistant rock. The softer rock is eroded more rapidly, producing a step.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which two processes are particularly important in undercutting the hard-rock ledge of a waterfall?
questions.explanation: Hydraulic action and abrasion deepen the plunge pool and undercut the hard-rock ledge, eventually contributing to collapse and waterfall retreat.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a plunge pool?

options.A: A shallow depression at the top of a mountain
options.B: A deep basin at the foot of a waterfall
options.C: A depositional ridge along a riverbank
options.D: A lake formed behind a coastal spit

questions.explanation: A plunge pool is a deep basin at the foot of a waterfall formed by falling water and the abrasion of rock fragments in turbulent water.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which process contributes to the deepening of a plunge pool?

options.A: Abrasion by rock fragments carried in turbulent water
options.D: Precipitation of calcium carbonate from cave water

questions.explanation: Rock fragments carried by turbulent water abrade the bed of the plunge pool, helping deepen the basin.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A gorge is best described as:
questions.explanation: A gorge is a narrow, steep-sided valley that may form through river incision or waterfall retreat.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How can the upstream retreat of a waterfall contribute to gorge formation?

options.A: By depositing coarse sediments at the river mouth
options.B: By enlarging a cave through groundwater solution
options.C: By building natural levees along both banks
options.D: By undercutting rock and causing collapse as the waterfall retreats

questions.explanation: Undercutting of rock followed by collapse allows a waterfall to retreat upstream, potentially leaving a narrow, steep-sided gorge.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a meander?

options.A: A winding bend or loop in a river channel
options.D: A cave formed by marine erosion

questions.explanation: A meander is a winding bend or loop in a river channel, commonly associated with erosion on its outer bank and deposition on its inner bank.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which part of a meander is generally associated with the greatest erosion?
questions.explanation: Faster flow and stronger erosion generally occur near the outer bank of a meander, producing a cut bank.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A point bar is generally formed on which part of a meander?
questions.explanation: A point bar is a depositional feature on the inner bank of a meander where sand and gravel accumulate.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which term describes the eroding outer bank of a meander?
questions.explanation: A cut bank is the eroding outer bank of a meander, whereas a point bar is the depositional inner bank.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which type of flow contributes to erosion along the outer bank and deposition along the inner bank of a meander?
questions.explanation: Helicoidal flow, together with faster flow near the outer bank, promotes outer-bank erosion and inner-bank sediment accumulation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What causes a meander bend to enlarge and migrate?

options.B: Differential velocity and erosion on the outer bank with deposition on the inner bank
options.D: Wind abrasion of the river bed

questions.explanation: Channel irregularities cause variations in velocity and pressure. Faster flow promotes outer-bank erosion while sediment accumulates on the inner bank, enlarging and migrating the bend.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: An ox-bow lake develops from which river feature?
questions.explanation: An ox-bow lake develops when a meander loop becomes cut off from the main river channel.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which event may enable a river to cut through the narrow neck of a meander?
questions.explanation: During a flood, a river may cut through the narrow neck of a meander and adopt a straighter course, abandoning the old loop.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which sequence correctly describes the formation of an ox-bow lake?

options.A: Meander-neck narrowing, river cut-off, deposition sealing the abandoned loop
options.B: Glacial plucking, moraine formation, meltwater erosion
options.C: Wind abrasion, dune migration, sand accumulation
options.D: Sea-cave formation, arch collapse, stack erosion

questions.explanation: Lateral erosion narrows the meander neck. A flood may cut through it, and deposition seals the ends of the abandoned loop, leaving a crescent-shaped ox-bow lake.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a floodplain?

options.B: A broad, relatively flat area beside a river
options.C: A ridge of sand in a desert
options.D: A rocky platform along a sea cliff

questions.explanation: A floodplain is a broad, relatively flat area beside a river, built through repeated overbank deposition, channel migration and sedimentation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which process contributes most directly to the repeated construction of floodplains?
questions.explanation: Repeated overbank deposition during floods, together with channel migration and associated sedimentation, builds floodplains.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A natural levee is:

options.B: A coastal ridge connecting an island to the mainland
options.D: A low ridge of sediment along a river bank

questions.explanation: A natural levee is a low sediment ridge formed along river banks through deposition during floods.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why is relatively coarse material deposited near river banks during flooding?

options.A: Floodwater loses velocity as it spills out of the channel
options.B: Wind speed increases near the channel
options.D: Glacial ice pushes sediments towards the banks

questions.explanation: When floodwater spills out of the channel, it loses velocity and deposits relatively coarse material near the banks, gradually building natural levees.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: An alluvial fan is generally formed where:

options.A: A river enters a deep sea
options.B: A stream emerges from a steep mountain valley onto a flatter plain

questions.explanation: An alluvial fan forms where a stream leaves a steep, confined mountain valley, loses velocity on reaching a flatter plain and spreads over a wider area.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Where is coarser sediment often deposited in an alluvial fan?
questions.explanation: Coarser material is often deposited near the apex of an alluvial fan, close to the point where the stream emerges from the mountain valley.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the principal difference between an alluvial fan and a delta?

options.A: Both form only through glacial deposition
options.B: An alluvial fan forms at a mountain valley exit, while a delta forms at a river mouth in standing water
options.C: A delta is always erosional, while an alluvial fan is always volcanic
options.D: An alluvial fan forms in the sea, while a delta forms in a desert

questions.explanation: An alluvial fan develops where a stream enters a flatter plain from a steep valley. A delta develops where a river enters a standing body of water and deposits sediment at its mouth.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A delta is primarily formed at:
questions.explanation: A delta forms at a river mouth when sediment accumulates as the river enters a sea, lake or another standing body of water and loses velocity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which combination influences the shape of a delta?

options.A: River sediment supply, waves, tides and currents
options.D: Rock hardness at the river source alone

questions.explanation: Delta shape depends on sediment supply from the river and the modifying influence of waves, tides and currents.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a commonly recognised descriptive type of delta?
questions.explanation: Common descriptive delta forms include arcuate, bird-foot or digitate, and cuspate deltas.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A bird-foot delta is also described as:
questions.explanation: Bird-foot and digitate are alternative names for a type of delta with finger-like projections.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which set represents the process-based classification of deltas?
questions.explanation: Process-based classification distinguishes river-dominated, wave-dominated and tide-dominated deltas.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a distributary?

options.A: A channel that branches away from the main river across a delta
options.B: A tributary that always flows towards the source

questions.explanation: A distributary branches away from the main river and carries water and sediment across a delta towards the sea or lake.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is an important Indian example of a major river delta?
questions.explanation: The Ganga–Brahmaputra delta is an important Indian example of a large river depositional landform.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Sundarbans are associated with which major geomorphic feature?
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans are associated with the Ganga–Brahmaputra delta.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Indo-Gangetic region is an important Indian example of which landform?
questions.explanation: The Indo-Gangetic region contains extensive floodplain landscapes formed through river sedimentation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Alluvial fans in India are particularly associated with which geographical setting?
questions.explanation: Alluvial fans occur along the Himalayan foothills where streams emerge from steep mountain valleys onto flatter plains.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which set of river-related landforms is identified in parts of the Ganga and Brahmaputra plains?
questions.explanation: Meanders and ox-bow lakes occur in parts of the Ganga and Brahmaputra plains.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Deeply incised valleys in India are particularly associated with:
questions.explanation: Deeply incised valleys are among the important river landforms found in Himalayan rivers.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Glacial landforms are created mainly by:

options.C: Moving glacier ice and associated meltwater

questions.explanation: Glacial landforms develop through erosion, transportation and deposition by moving glacier ice and associated meltwater.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A cirque, corrie or cwm is:

options.B: A steep-sided, armchair-shaped hollow at the head of a glacial valley

questions.explanation: Cirque, corrie and cwm are alternative terms for a steep-sided, armchair-shaped hollow at the head of a glacial valley.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which combination of processes may enlarge a cirque?

options.A: Longshore drift, hydraulic action and wave refraction
options.C: River deposition and overbank flooding only
options.D: Plucking, abrasion, freeze-thaw weathering and nivation

questions.explanation: Cirques may be enlarged by glacial plucking and abrasion, freeze-thaw weathering and nivation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a tarn?

options.A: A small mountain lake occupying a cirque after glacier retreat
options.C: A river channel across a delta

questions.explanation: A tarn is a small mountain lake occupying a cirque or corrie after the glacier retreats.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are moraines?

options.C: Ridges or accumulations of debris transported and deposited by glaciers

questions.explanation: Moraines are ridges or accumulations of glacial debris. They consist of till and may contain particles ranging from clay to boulders.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The material deposited directly by glacier ice in moraines is commonly known as:
questions.explanation: Moraines consist of till, which is glacial debris containing a wide range of particle sizes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A lateral moraine is deposited:

options.A: At the centre of a delta
options.B: Along the side of a valley glacier
options.C: At the foot of a sea cliff
options.D: On the floor of a limestone cave

questions.explanation: A lateral moraine is a ridge of glacial debris deposited along the side of a valley glacier.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A medial moraine commonly develops when:

options.C: The lateral moraines of two tributary glaciers join
options.D: Two desert dunes move in opposite directions

questions.explanation: A medial moraine commonly forms when the lateral moraines of two tributary glaciers join near the middle of the combined glacier.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A terminal or end moraine marks:

options.A: The maximum extent reached by a glacier during an advance
options.B: The centre of a valley glacier
options.C: The starting point of a river
options.D: The boundary of a coastal lagoon

questions.explanation: A terminal or end moraine is deposited at the farthest advance of a glacier and marks its maximum extent during that advance.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A ridge of debris deposited during a temporary pause or minor readvance of a retreating glacier is called:
questions.explanation: A recessional moraine forms during a temporary pause or minor readvance while a glacier is retreating.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a ground moraine?

options.A: A ridge deposited at the maximum glacier advance
options.B: A widespread layer of till deposited beneath or left behind by glacier ice
options.C: A ridge of stratified meltwater gravel
options.D: A streamlined ridge formed by wind erosion

questions.explanation: Ground moraine is a widespread layer of till deposited beneath or left behind by glacier ice, often producing gently undulating terrain.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A drumlin is best described as:

options.A: A steep-sided hollow at the head of a glacier
options.C: An elongated, streamlined hill composed mainly of glacial sediment
options.D: A long ridge of wind-blown silt

questions.explanation: A drumlin is an elongated, streamlined hill mainly composed of glacial sediment and commonly aligned with former ice flow.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about drumlin formation is most accurate according to the study material?

options.A: Drumlins are exclusively formed by marine erosion
options.B: Their formation mechanisms are complex and may involve subglacial deposition and deformation
options.C: They are always formed by volcanic eruptions
options.D: They are exclusively made of wind-blown silt

questions.explanation: Drumlin formation is complex and may involve subglacial deposition and deformation. They are commonly aligned with former ice flow.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is an esker?

options.A: A long, winding ridge of stratified sand and gravel

questions.explanation: An esker is a long, winding ridge of stratified sand and gravel deposited by meltwater streams within or beneath a glacier.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which agent deposits the stratified sand and gravel that forms an esker?
questions.explanation: Eskers are deposited by meltwater streams flowing within or beneath a glacier.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which comparison between moraine and esker is correct?

options.A: Both are formed exclusively by wind deposition
options.B: Moraine consists of direct ice-laid debris, whereas esker consists of meltwater-laid stratified sand and gravel
options.C: Moraine is a coastal feature, whereas esker is a karst feature
options.D: Moraine is made only of clay, whereas esker is made only of boulders

questions.explanation: Moraines are direct ice-laid accumulations of generally unsorted till, whereas eskers are stratified sand and gravel deposits formed by glacial meltwater.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A U-shaped valley is also known as:
questions.explanation: A U-shaped valley is also called a glacial trough and is produced by glacial widening, deepening and straightening of a pre-existing river valley.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which feature distinguishes a typical U-shaped valley from a V-shaped valley?

options.A: A U-shaped valley has a broader floor and steep sides
options.B: A U-shaped valley is always formed by wind
options.C: A U-shaped valley has no valley floor
options.D: A U-shaped valley is formed exclusively by marine deposition

questions.explanation: A glacial U-shaped valley has a broad floor and steep sides, whereas a V-shaped valley is commonly produced by river downcutting and slope processes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: An arête is:

options.C: A sharp ridge between adjacent cirques or glacial valleys

questions.explanation: An arête is a sharp ridge separating adjacent cirques or glacial valleys.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A glacial horn is:

options.B: A sharp pyramidal peak formed by the erosion of several cirques
options.C: A ridge of stratified meltwater gravel

questions.explanation: A horn is a sharp pyramidal peak formed when several cirques erode back towards one another.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes an arête from a horn?

options.A: An arête is a lake, while a horn is a moraine
options.B: An arête is a depositional ridge, while a horn is a dune
options.D: An arête is a sharp ridge, while a horn is a pyramidal peak

questions.explanation: An arête is a sharp ridge between adjacent cirques or valleys, while a horn is a pyramidal mountain peak formed by erosion from several cirques.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why is a hanging valley left at a higher elevation than the main glacial trough?

options.A: The tributary glacier erodes more deeply than the main glacier
options.B: The main glacier erodes more deeply than the tributary glacier
options.C: Sea waves raise the tributary valley
options.D: Wind deposits a thick layer of loess

questions.explanation: The main glacier commonly erodes its valley more deeply than the tributary glacier, leaving the tributary valley at a higher elevation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which feature may commonly occur at the outlet of a hanging valley?
questions.explanation: Because a hanging valley lies above the main glacial trough, waterfalls may occur at its outlet.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A fjord is:

options.C: A deep, narrow, steep-sided glacial valley flooded by seawater

questions.explanation: A fjord is a glacial valley that becomes flooded by seawater after glacier retreat and marine inundation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which Indian mountain system contains important examples of cirques, moraines, U-shaped valleys and hanging valleys?
questions.explanation: The Himalaya contains numerous glacial landforms, including cirques, moraines, U-shaped valleys, hanging valleys and glacial lakes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group contains regions where glacial landforms are especially evident in India?

options.A: Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh
options.B: Goa, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Lakshadweep
options.C: Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab, Gujarat and Delhi
options.D: Odisha, Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal and Chhattisgarh

questions.explanation: Glacial landforms are especially evident in high-altitude areas of Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Aeolian landforms are produced by:
questions.explanation: Aeolian landforms are produced by wind erosion, transportation and deposition, especially in dry and sparsely vegetated environments.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Aeolian landforms are particularly common in:

options.C: Deserts and dry, sparsely vegetated environments

questions.explanation: Wind action is particularly effective in deserts and other dry environments with sparse vegetation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A mushroom rock is also known as:
questions.explanation: Mushroom rock is also called pedestal rock because it commonly has a narrow base and a broader upper part.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why is a mushroom rock commonly narrower near its base?

options.A: Sea waves erode its upper part
options.C: Wind-driven sand abrades the lower part more intensely
options.D: Groundwater dissolves the lower part in every case

questions.explanation: Wind-driven sand tends to travel close to the ground, concentrating abrasion on the lower part of the rock and producing undercutting.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about mushroom rock formation is correct?

options.A: It is produced exclusively by chemical precipitation
options.B: Wind abrasion near ground level is important, but rock structure and differential weathering may also influence its shape
options.C: It is formed only by glacial deposition
options.D: It develops from the collapse of a sea arch

questions.explanation: Wind abrasion concentrated near the ground is a major factor, although rock structure and differential weathering may also affect the shape of pedestal rocks.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a yardang?

options.A: A long, streamlined ridge carved by persistent wind erosion
options.B: A small lake in a cirque
options.C: A ridge of sand deposited across a bay
options.D: A depositional feature at a river mouth

questions.explanation: A yardang is a long, streamlined ridge carved in softer rock or sediment by persistent wind abrasion and deflation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Yardangs are generally aligned with:

options.C: The direction of glacial movement only

questions.explanation: Yardangs are generally aligned with the prevailing effective wind direction that shapes them through abrasion and deflation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A zeugen is primarily associated with:

options.A: Differential wind erosion of alternating hard and soft rock layers

questions.explanation: Zeugen develops through differential wind erosion of alternating hard and soft rock layers, leaving resistant caprock and ridge-like forms.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which feature is most strongly controlled by alternating hard and soft rock strata?
questions.explanation: Zeugen is strongly controlled by alternating resistant and less resistant rock layers. Softer layers are removed more readily, leaving resistant caprock and ridges.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a yardang from a zeugen?

options.A: A yardang is a streamlined wind-carved ridge, while a zeugen is a strata-controlled tabular or ridge-like feature
options.B: A yardang is a coastal depositional feature, while a zeugen is a glacial lake
options.C: Both are formed exclusively by groundwater solution
options.D: A yardang is a dune, while a zeugen is a delta

questions.explanation: Yardangs are streamlined wind-eroded ridges generally aligned with the effective wind direction. Zeugens are strongly influenced by alternating hard and soft strata and undercutting.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A barchan dune has which characteristic shape?
questions.explanation: A barchan is a crescent-shaped sand dune commonly formed under relatively constant wind direction and limited sand supply.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Under which conditions does a typical barchan dune develop?

options.B: Heavy rainfall and continuous river flooding
options.C: Limited sand supply and relatively constant wind direction

questions.explanation: Barchans commonly form where sand supply is limited and wind direction is relatively constant.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The horns of a typical barchan dune point:
questions.explanation: The horns of a barchan dune extend in the downwind direction, while its steep slip face generally lies on the lee side.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The steep slip face of a barchan dune is generally located on which side?
questions.explanation: The steep slip face of a barchan is generally on the lee side, while its horns point downwind.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A seif dune is also called a:
questions.explanation: A seif dune is also known as a longitudinal dune and forms a long, narrow ridge of sand broadly parallel to the resultant prevailing wind direction.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which condition commonly influences the development of seif dunes?

options.B: Winds from more than one direction influencing dune growth

questions.explanation: Seif dunes commonly develop where winds from more than one direction influence dune growth, producing long ridges broadly parallel to the resultant prevailing wind.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is loess?
questions.explanation: Loess is a widespread deposit of wind-blown silt that is generally fine-grained, porous and often fertile.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which region is a classic example of extensive loess deposits?
questions.explanation: The Loess Plateau of China is a classic example of extensive wind-blown silt deposits.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main difference between loess and dune sand?

options.A: Loess is made mainly of gravel, whereas dunes are made of clay
options.B: Both are exclusively formed by glacial ice
options.C: Loess is predominantly wind-blown silt, whereas dunes are mainly composed of sand
options.D: Loess is marine sediment, whereas dunes are river deposits

questions.explanation: Loess is predominantly wind-blown silt deposited in blanket-like accumulations, whereas dunes are mounds or ridges composed mainly of sand.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which dune type generally forms at right angles to the prevailing wind?
questions.explanation: Transverse dunes form broadly at right angles to the prevailing wind direction.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which characteristic is associated with parabolic dunes?

options.B: They are always formed beneath glaciers
options.C: Their arms point upwind and they are often stabilised by vegetation
options.D: They consist of stratified glacial gravel

questions.explanation: Parabolic dunes are often stabilised by vegetation and have arms pointing upwind, unlike barchan horns which point downwind.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Star dunes are generally associated with:
questions.explanation: Star dunes have several arms and generally form under multidirectional wind conditions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which comparison between barchan and parabolic dunes is correct?

options.B: Barchan horns point downwind, whereas parabolic dune arms point upwind
options.C: Barchans are glacial, whereas parabolic dunes are marine
options.D: Both are formed by groundwater precipitation

questions.explanation: Barchan horns extend downwind, whereas the arms of parabolic dunes point upwind. This is an important examination distinction.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which Indian desert is an important example of aeolian landforms?
questions.explanation: The Thar Desert of Rajasthan contains barchans, other dune forms, wind-shaped rock surfaces and extensive aeolian sand deposits.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about loess in the Indian Thar Desert is correct according to the study material?

options.A: It is the dominant characteristic landform of the Thar
options.B: It is more extensive than the Loess Plateau of China
options.C: It is a major glacial deposit
options.D: It is not a characteristic major landform of the Indian Thar comparable to China's Loess Plateau

questions.explanation: The Thar contains extensive aeolian sand and dune deposits, but loess is not a characteristic major landform there comparable to China's Loess Plateau.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Coastal landforms are shaped by:

options.A: Waves, tides, currents, erosion, sediment transport and deposition

questions.explanation: Coastal landforms develop through the combined influence of waves, tides, currents, coastal erosion, sediment transport and deposition.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Coastal landforms are broadly classified into which two categories?
questions.explanation: Coastal landforms may be erosional or depositional depending on the dominant marine processes involved.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A sea cliff is primarily formed by:
questions.explanation: A sea cliff is a steep coastal rock face formed mainly by wave erosion at its base, undercutting and subsequent collapse.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A wave-cut notch develops:

options.A: At the foot of a sea cliff
options.B: At the summit of a mountain
options.C: At the centre of a desert dune

questions.explanation: A wave-cut notch is a recess eroded at the foot of a sea cliff by wave action, particularly hydraulic action and abrasion.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the significance of a wave-cut notch in the development of a sea cliff?

options.A: It increases the accumulation of glacial till
options.D: It undercuts the cliff and encourages collapse

questions.explanation: Wave action creates a notch at the cliff base. Continued undercutting weakens the cliff and encourages collapse and retreat.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A wave-cut platform is:

options.B: A gently seaward-sloping rocky surface left by retreating sea cliffs
options.D: A depositional ridge across a river delta

questions.explanation: A wave-cut platform is a gently seaward-sloping rocky surface left as a cliff retreats through repeated undercutting and collapse.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which sequence is associated with the formation of a wave-cut platform?

options.A: Wind deposition, dune migration and vegetation growth
options.B: Glacial plucking, moraine deposition and ice retreat
options.C: Cliff undercutting, collapse and continued cliff retreat

questions.explanation: Repeated wave undercutting and collapse cause a sea cliff to retreat, leaving a gently sloping rocky wave-cut platform.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Sea caves commonly develop when waves exploit:

options.A: Joints, faults and other weaknesses in a headland

questions.explanation: Waves exploit joints, faults and other weaknesses in a headland. Hydraulic action and abrasion enlarge the openings into caves.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A sea arch forms when:

options.A: A glacier deposits sediment across a valley
options.B: A river cuts through a meander neck
options.C: A cave is enlarged through a headland until it cuts through to the other side

questions.explanation: A sea arch develops when marine erosion enlarges a cave through a headland until it opens on the other side.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A sea stack is formed by:

options.A: Deposition of sediment across a bay
options.B: Collapse of the roof of a sea arch
options.C: Deposition of till beneath a glacier

questions.explanation: When the roof of a sea arch collapses, an isolated pillar of rock remains offshore or near the coast. This is called a sea stack.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a stump in coastal geomorphology?

options.C: A low remnant of a stack after continued erosion

questions.explanation: A stump is a low remnant of a sea stack left after continued wave erosion and collapse. It may be visible mainly at low tide.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the correct chronological sequence of coastal erosional features?
questions.explanation: Wave erosion enlarges a weakness into a cave, continued erosion forms an arch, roof collapse leaves a stack and further erosion lowers it to a stump.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A beach is primarily:

options.A: An accumulation of sediment along the shore

questions.explanation: A beach is a depositional accumulation of sand, shingle, pebbles or other sediment along the shore.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which processes help shape beaches?
questions.explanation: Beaches are shaped by waves, tides and currents acting on sediment accumulated along the shore.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A spit is usually attached to the mainland at:
questions.explanation: A spit is a narrow ridge of sand or shingle attached to the mainland at one end and extending into a bay or estuary.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which process commonly contributes to spit formation?
questions.explanation: Longshore drift transports and deposits sand or shingle along the coast, commonly forming spits.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A coastal bar is:

options.B: A ridge of sand or shingle deposited across a bay or inlet

questions.explanation: A bar is a ridge of sand or shingle deposited across a bay or inlet. It may connect headlands and partly or completely enclose a water body.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A tombolo is a depositional feature that connects:

options.C: An island to the mainland or another island
options.D: A desert dune to a river

questions.explanation: A tombolo is a depositional ridge or bar connecting an island to the mainland or to another island.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a lagoon?

options.A: A shallow water body separated from the open sea by a coastal barrier

questions.explanation: A lagoon is a shallow water body separated from the open sea by a spit, bar, barrier island or reef, often with a restricted sea connection.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How can longshore drift and wave action contribute to lagoon formation?

options.B: By depositing sediment that partly or completely encloses shallow coastal water
options.D: By transporting glacial till into caves

questions.explanation: Longshore drift and wave action may deposit sediment across a bay or along a coast. This partly or completely encloses shallow coastal water, creating a lagoon.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a spit from a bar?

options.A: A spit is attached at one end, whereas a bar extends across a bay or inlet
options.B: A spit is always underwater, whereas a bar is always a cliff
options.C: A spit is glacial, whereas a bar is fluvial

questions.explanation: A spit is attached to land at one end and projects into water. A bar extends across a bay or inlet and may join two sides, enclosing a lagoon.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Chilika Lake is located in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Chilika Lake is located in Odisha and is an important example of a brackish coastal lagoon.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Chilika Lake is separated from which water body by a barrier or spit system?
questions.explanation: Chilika is a major brackish coastal lagoon separated from the Bay of Bengal by a barrier/spit system.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which beach is cited as a familiar example of a coastal landform in India?
questions.explanation: Marina Beach is a familiar coastal example mentioned in the study material. Beaches, spits, bars and lagoons occur along both Indian coasts.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about Indian coastal depositional features is correct?

options.A: They occur only along the western coast
options.B: They occur only along the eastern coast
options.C: Spits and lagoons are exclusively glacial features
options.D: Beaches, spits, bars and lagoons occur along both eastern and western coasts

questions.explanation: Beaches, spits, bars and lagoons occur along both India's eastern and western coasts, although individual features may change over time.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Karst topography is primarily associated with:

options.B: Dissolution of soluble rocks by groundwater and surface water

questions.explanation: Karst topography develops mainly through the dissolution of soluble rocks by groundwater and surface water.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group contains rocks commonly associated with karst development?
questions.explanation: Karst landscapes commonly develop in soluble rocks such as limestone, dolomite and gypsum.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which combination is characteristic of karst terrain?

options.A: Sinkholes, caves, underground streams and limited surface drainage

questions.explanation: Karst terrain commonly contains sinkholes, caves and underground streams, with limited surface drainage because water enters subterranean openings.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which substance does rainwater absorb to form weak carbonic acid?
questions.explanation: Rainwater absorbs carbon dioxide from the air and soil, producing weak carbonic acid that contributes to limestone dissolution.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Through which geological openings does slightly acidic water commonly penetrate limestone?
questions.explanation: Water percolates through joints and bedding planes in limestone, dissolving calcite and enlarging openings into conduits and caves.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A sinkhole is also known as:
questions.explanation: A sinkhole, also called a doline, is a closed depression characteristic of karst terrain.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which combination of processes can form a sinkhole?

options.C: Dissolution, cave-roof collapse and gradual subsidence

questions.explanation: Sinkholes may form through dissolution, collapse of a cave roof or gradual subsidence into underground openings.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Limestone caves are primarily formed through:
questions.explanation: Slightly acidic groundwater dissolves limestone along joints, bedding planes and fractures, creating underground cavities and passages.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which geological structures provide pathways for the development of limestone caves?
questions.explanation: Groundwater dissolves limestone along joints, bedding planes and fractures, which can enlarge into extensive interconnected cave systems.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is underground drainage?

options.A: A system in which surface water enters subterranean conduits and caves
options.B: A river system that flows only above ground
options.C: A coastal current flowing parallel to the shore
options.D: A drainage system formed exclusively by glaciers

questions.explanation: Underground drainage occurs when surface water enters sinkholes or swallow holes and flows through subterranean conduits and caves instead of remaining in surface streams.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a swallow hole?

options.A: A hole in a coastal cliff
options.B: An opening through which a surface stream disappears underground
options.C: A hollow formed by wind erosion
options.D: A depression at the head of a glacier

questions.explanation: A swallow hole is an opening through which surface water disappears underground into a cave or subterranean drainage system.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A stalactite develops:

options.D: Along the crest of a sand dune

questions.explanation: Stalactites are calcium carbonate deposits that hang from cave ceilings, formed when dripping water loses carbon dioxide and precipitates calcite.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A stalagmite develops:

options.D: At the end of a glacier

questions.explanation: Stalagmites grow upward from cave floors as dripping water deposits calcium carbonate.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which memory aid correctly distinguishes stalactites and stalagmites?

options.A: Stalactites hold tight to the ceiling; stalagmites might grow up from the ground
options.B: Stalactites grow upward; stalagmites hang downward
options.C: Both grow exclusively on cave walls
options.D: Both are formed by wind abrasion

questions.explanation: Stalactites hang from the ceiling, while stalagmites rise from the ground. The memory aids help distinguish their positions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which process is primarily responsible for the growth of stalactites and stalagmites?

options.D: Precipitation of calcium carbonate from cave water

questions.explanation: Water containing dissolved calcium bicarbonate enters caves. Loss of carbon dioxide and evaporation can cause calcium carbonate to precipitate, producing stalactites and stalagmites.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What may eventually happen when a stalactite and a stalagmite continue growing towards one another?

options.A: They may join to form a column
options.C: They may become a natural levee
options.D: They may form a sea arch

questions.explanation: Stalactites grow downwards from the ceiling and stalagmites upwards from the floor. They may eventually meet and form a column.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Stalactites and stalagmites are classified as:
questions.explanation: Stalactites and stalagmites are depositional features formed through precipitation of calcium carbonate, even though the caves themselves are commonly produced by dissolution.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes cave formation from stalactite formation?

options.A: Both are exclusively produced by wind erosion
options.B: Caves are deposited by glaciers, while stalactites are formed by rivers
options.C: Caves commonly form by groundwater dissolution, whereas stalactites form by calcium carbonate precipitation
options.D: Both are produced by marine abrasion

questions.explanation: Limestone caves are commonly formed through groundwater dissolution. Stalactites and stalagmites are deposited later through calcium carbonate precipitation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a karst window?

options.A: An opening where an underground drainage system or subterranean stream becomes exposed at the surface
options.B: A closed depression formed by wind erosion
options.C: A coastal opening in a sea arch

questions.explanation: A karst window exposes a subterranean stream or part of an underground drainage system at the surface, often due to roof collapse or erosion.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which Indian state is particularly known for extensive limestone cave systems?
questions.explanation: Meghalaya has extensive limestone cave systems, including caves in the Khasi and Jaintia Hills.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The extensive limestone cave systems of Meghalaya are especially associated with which hills?
questions.explanation: The Khasi and Jaintia Hills of Meghalaya contain extensive limestone cave systems.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Apart from Meghalaya, limestone caves are also found in parts of which Indian states according to the study material?
questions.explanation: Limestone caves also occur in parts of Andhra Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh. Their formation depends on soluble rock and groundwater circulation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which set contains only river erosional landforms?

options.B: Alluvial fan, point bar and delta

questions.explanation: V-shaped valleys, waterfalls and gorges are river erosional landforms. Floodplains, levees, fans, point bars and deltas are depositional features.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group contains river depositional landforms?

options.B: Floodplains, natural levees, alluvial fans, point bars and deltas

questions.explanation: Floodplains, levees, alluvial fans, point bars and deltas are important river depositional landforms.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group contains only glacial erosional features?

options.C: Cirques, arêtes, horns and U-shaped valleys

questions.explanation: Cirques, arêtes, horns and U-shaped valleys are glacial erosional features. Moraines, drumlins and eskers are depositional or accumulation features.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a glacial depositional or accumulation feature?
questions.explanation: An esker is a glacial meltwater-deposited ridge of stratified sand and gravel. Arêtes, horns and cirques are erosional features.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which pair consists entirely of wind erosional landforms?
questions.explanation: Mushroom rocks and yardangs are produced mainly by wind erosion. Dunes and loess are depositional features.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group contains wind depositional landforms?
questions.explanation: Barchans, seif dunes, other dune forms and loess are wind-depositional features.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which set contains coastal erosional landforms?

options.B: Sea cliffs, caves, arches and stacks

questions.explanation: Sea cliffs, caves, arches and stacks are produced by coastal erosion. Beaches, spits, bars, tombolos and lagoons are depositional features.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group contains only coastal depositional landforms?
questions.explanation: Beaches, spits, bars, tombolos and lagoons are coastal depositional landforms.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which pairing correctly identifies the dominant process responsible for the formation of the features?

options.A: Sinkhole – groundwater dissolution; stalactite – calcium carbonate precipitation
options.B: Sinkhole – wind deposition; stalactite – glacial abrasion
options.C: Sinkhole – marine deposition; stalactite – river erosion
options.D: Sinkhole – glacial deposition; stalactite – wind deflation

questions.explanation: Sinkholes and limestone caves commonly result from dissolution, whereas stalactites and stalagmites form through precipitation of calcium carbonate.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following pairs is incorrectly matched?

options.C: Esker – Direct deposition of unsorted till by glacier ice

questions.explanation: An esker consists of stratified sand and gravel deposited by meltwater streams. Direct ice-laid, generally unsorted debris is associated with moraines.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?

options.A: The outer bank of a meander is generally erosional
options.B: The inner bank of a meander is generally depositional

questions.explanation: Parabolic dune arms point upwind, whereas barchan horns point downwind. The remaining statements are correct.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which pair of features is correctly matched with the environment of formation?

options.A: Fjord – Glacial valley flooded by seawater

questions.explanation: A fjord is a deep, narrow glacial valley flooded by seawater after glacier retreat. The other pairs incorrectly identify the geomorphic agent.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is correctly matched?

options.A: Alluvial fan – River mouth in standing water
options.C: Alluvial fan – Stream leaving a steep valley for a flatter plain

questions.explanation: An alluvial fan forms where a stream emerges from a steep mountain valley onto a flatter plain. A delta forms at a river mouth in standing water.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a glacial erosional landform?
questions.explanation: Moraines are accumulations of glacial debris and are depositional features. Cirques, arêtes and horns are glacial erosional landforms.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which feature is incorrectly classified as an erosional coastal landform?
questions.explanation: A beach is a depositional feature formed by the accumulation of sediment along the shore. Caves, arches and cliffs are erosional coastal features.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement should be considered when classifying a landform by its dominant agent?

options.A: Every landform is formed by exactly one process
options.C: Some landforms are polygenetic and may involve multiple processes
options.D: Only endogenic processes shape the Earth's surface

questions.explanation: Some landforms are polygenetic, meaning that more than one geomorphic process contributes to their development. A feature should not automatically be assigned to only one process in every setting.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which set correctly lists the five major geomorphic landform groups covered in the chapter?

options.A: Volcanic, tectonic, biological, atmospheric and industrial
options.B: Fluvial, glacial, aeolian, coastal/marine and karst
options.C: Mountain, plateau, plain, island and ocean
options.D: Continental, oceanic, volcanic, tectonic and biological

questions.explanation: The five groups covered are fluvial, glacial, aeolian, coastal/marine and karst landforms.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are outwash deposits?
questions.explanation: Outwash deposits are accumulations of sediment transported and deposited by glacial meltwater.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A deflation hollow is associated with which geomorphic process?

options.B: Removal of loose surface material by wind

questions.explanation: Deflation is the removal of loose particles by wind. Deflation hollows are erosional depressions produced by this process.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Flowstone is associated with which type of geomorphic environment?
questions.explanation: Flowstone is a calcium carbonate cave deposit formed through precipitation from flowing or seeping mineral-rich water.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a depositional feature of groundwater geomorphology?
