questions.explanation: Cave columns develop when stalactites and stalagmites join through calcium carbonate deposition. Sinkholes, caves and underground conduits are associated mainly with dissolution.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which chemical substance is deposited to form stalactites and stalagmites?
questions.explanation: Calcium carbonate precipitates from mineral-rich cave water, producing stalactites, stalagmites and related cave deposits.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about the sediment distribution of an alluvial fan is correct?

options.A: Coarser material is often deposited near the apex
options.B: Only fine clay is deposited near the apex
options.C: All sediment is transported directly into the sea
options.D: No sediment deposition occurs near the mountain valley exit

questions.explanation: As a stream emerges from a steep mountain valley and loses velocity on a flatter plain, coarser material is often deposited near the apex of the alluvial fan.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which feature is formed by sediment accumulation along the inner bank of a meandering river?
questions.explanation: Slower flow along the inner bank encourages sediment deposition, creating a point bar.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which glacial feature commonly consists of a wide range of particle sizes, from clay to boulders?
questions.explanation: Till deposited by glacier ice may contain particles ranging from clay to boulders and is generally unsorted.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What happens to a cirque after glacier retreat if water occupies the hollow?
questions.explanation: A tarn is a small mountain lake occupying a cirque or corrie after the glacier retreats.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which processes are specifically responsible for enlarging weaknesses in a coastal headland into sea caves?
questions.explanation: Hydraulic action and abrasion enlarge joints, faults and other weaknesses in a headland into sea caves.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between a bar and a lagoon?

options.A: A bar always destroys a lagoon
options.B: A lagoon forms only through glacial erosion
options.C: A bar may partly or completely enclose coastal water, forming a lagoon
options.D: A lagoon is a type of sea cliff

questions.explanation: A coastal bar can extend across a bay or inlet and partly or completely enclose a water body, creating a lagoon.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why is surface drainage often limited in karst terrain?

options.A: Rainfall never occurs in limestone regions
options.B: Water frequently enters sinkholes and underground drainage passages
options.D: Glaciers permanently cover all limestone regions

questions.explanation: In karst terrain, surface water can enter sinkholes and swallow holes and flow through subterranean conduits and caves rather than remaining in surface streams.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A fjord is created when which type of pre-existing valley is flooded?
questions.explanation: A fjord forms when a deep glacial valley becomes flooded by seawater following glacier retreat and marine inundation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which combination correctly identifies three important depositional dune types other than barchans?
questions.explanation: Transverse dunes form broadly at right angles to prevailing wind, parabolic dunes often have vegetation-stabilised arms pointing upwind, and star dunes have several arms under multidirectional winds.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following factors is NOT sufficient on its own to determine the shape of a river delta?

options.D: The colour of the river water

questions.explanation: Delta shape depends on sediment supply, waves, tides and currents. Water colour is not identified as a controlling factor in the study material.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which moraine is commonly associated with the joining of lateral moraines from two tributary glaciers?
questions.explanation: When two tributary glaciers join, their lateral moraines may combine to form a medial moraine near the middle of the glacier.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement is the most accurate approach to studying landforms for geographical examinations?

options.B: Study the agent, formation process, diagnostic shape and erosional or depositional nature
options.C: Assume all landforms have one universal formation mechanism

questions.explanation: The study material emphasises learning the geomorphic agent, process, diagnostic shape and whether the feature is erosional or depositional. Detailed formation models and terminology may vary among textbooks.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which combination best explains why the dominant river process changes from one part of a river system to another?

options.A: Only the colour and temperature of water
options.B: Gradient, discharge, sediment load, channel form and geology
options.C: Only the altitude of the river source
options.D: Only the amount of vegetation along the banks

questions.explanation: The dominant river process depends on interacting factors such as gradient, discharge, sediment load, channel form and underlying geology.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which statement about the upper, middle and lower courses of a river is most accurate?

options.A: Each course has a fixed boundary and only one geomorphic process
options.B: Vertical erosion occurs exclusively in the upper course
options.C: They represent general patterns of changing processes rather than rigid divisions
options.D: Deposition never occurs in the upper course

questions.explanation: The upper, middle and lower course divisions describe general tendencies in gradient, erosion and deposition; they are not rigid boundaries.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A river follows a winding path around alternating projecting ridges instead of cutting directly through them. Which landform is represented?
questions.explanation: Interlocking spurs are projecting ridges of resistant land around which a young river winds along the path of least resistance.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which sequence correctly describes the development of a waterfall-associated gorge?

options.A: Deposition of sand, formation of a delta and flooding
options.B: Differential erosion, plunge-pool development, undercutting and collapse, followed by waterfall retreat
options.C: Wind abrasion, dune formation and deflation
options.D: Limestone dissolution, stalactite formation and cave collapse

questions.explanation: Differential erosion creates the waterfall step. Falling water and abrasion deepen the plunge pool, undercut the ledge and cause collapse. Continued retreat may leave a gorge.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: During a flood, a river cuts through the narrow neck of a meander. What happens to the former meander loop?

options.C: It may become an isolated ox-bow lake after deposition seals its ends
options.D: It develops into a natural levee

questions.explanation: After the river cuts through the meander neck and adopts a straighter course, deposition may seal the ends of the abandoned loop, leaving an ox-bow lake.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which process contributes to the development of a floodplain besides repeated overbank deposition?
questions.explanation: Floodplains develop through repeated overbank deposition, channel migration and associated sedimentation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Why is relatively coarse sediment commonly deposited near the apex of an alluvial fan?

options.A: The stream gains velocity after reaching the plain
options.B: The stream loses velocity as it emerges from a steep valley and spreads out
options.C: Sea waves push coarse sediment inland

questions.explanation: When a stream leaves a steep, confined valley and enters a flatter plain, it loses velocity and spreads out. Coarser material is often deposited near the fan apex.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which factor combination influences the shape of a river delta?

options.A: Only the temperature of the river water
options.B: Only the altitude of the river source
options.C: River sediment supply, waves, tides and currents

questions.explanation: Delta shape depends on the amount of sediment supplied by the river and the modifying effects of waves, tides and currents.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes a distributary?

options.A: A tributary that joins the main river in its upper course
options.B: A channel that branches away from the main river across a delta
options.C: An underground stream in limestone terrain
options.D: A temporary stream flowing down a desert dune

questions.explanation: A distributary branches away from the main river and carries water and sediment across a delta towards the sea or lake.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which set of processes can contribute to the enlargement of a cirque?

options.A: Plucking, abrasion, freeze-thaw weathering and nivation
options.B: Longshore drift, wave refraction and deposition
options.D: River overbank flooding and natural levee formation

questions.explanation: Cirques are enlarged by glacial plucking and abrasion, along with freeze-thaw weathering and nivation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Two tributary glaciers merge. Which glacial depositional feature may develop where their lateral moraines join?
questions.explanation: A medial moraine commonly forms when the lateral moraines of two tributary glaciers join near the middle of the combined glacier.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A ridge of glacial debris marks the farthest advance of a glacier during a particular advance. What is it called?
questions.explanation: A terminal or end moraine is deposited at the farthest extent reached by a glacier during that advance.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A glacier temporarily pauses or makes a minor readvance while retreating, leaving a ridge of debris. Which feature is formed?
questions.explanation: A recessional moraine is deposited during a temporary pause or minor readvance in the overall retreat of a glacier.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which description best identifies a ground moraine?

options.A: A sharp ridge between two cirques
options.B: A widespread layer of till left beneath or behind glacier ice
options.C: A winding ridge of stratified meltwater sediment
options.D: A pyramidal peak formed by several cirques

questions.explanation: Ground moraine is a widespread deposit of till left beneath or behind glacier ice and may produce gently undulating terrain.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which statement about drumlins is correct?

options.A: They are crescent-shaped dunes formed by wind
options.B: They are elongated, streamlined hills composed mainly of glacial sediment
options.C: They are deep coastal valleys flooded by seawater
options.D: They are limestone deposits hanging from cave ceilings

questions.explanation: Drumlins are elongated, streamlined hills composed mainly of glacial sediment and commonly aligned with former ice flow.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is the principal material deposited in an esker?

options.A: Unsorted boulders deposited directly by ice
options.B: Stratified sand and gravel deposited by meltwater streams

questions.explanation: Eskers are winding ridges of stratified sand and gravel deposited by meltwater streams flowing within or beneath a glacier.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Why may waterfalls occur at the outlet of a hanging valley?

options.A: The tributary glacier eroded more deeply than the main glacier
options.B: The main glacier eroded its valley more deeply than the tributary glacier
options.C: Wind deposited a dune across the valley
options.D: A sea arch collapsed at the valley outlet

questions.explanation: The main glacier generally erodes its trough more deeply than a tributary glacier. The tributary valley is therefore left at a higher elevation, and a waterfall may occur at its outlet.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which combination of conditions is most favourable for the formation of barchan dunes?

options.A: Abundant sand, dense vegetation and multidirectional winds
options.B: Limited sand supply and relatively constant wind direction
options.C: Permanent waterlogging and strong tidal currents
options.D: Thick ice cover and frequent glacier movement

questions.explanation: Barchan dunes are crescent-shaped dunes that commonly form where sand supply is limited and wind direction is relatively constant.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a parabolic dune from a barchan dune?

options.A: Parabolic dune arms point upwind, whereas barchan horns point downwind
options.B: Both always have horns pointing downwind
options.C: Parabolic dunes form only under glaciers
options.D: Barchan dunes are composed mainly of wind-blown silt

questions.explanation: Parabolic dunes are often stabilised by vegetation and have arms pointing upwind, whereas the horns of barchan dunes point downwind.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which dune type is characterised by several arms and is associated with winds from multiple directions?
questions.explanation: Star dunes have several arms and commonly form where winds from multiple directions influence dune growth.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is the characteristic orientation of transverse dunes in relation to the prevailing wind?

options.A: Broadly parallel to the prevailing wind
options.B: Broadly at right angles to the prevailing wind
options.D: Always arranged in a circular pattern

questions.explanation: Transverse dunes form broadly at right angles to the prevailing wind direction.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which sequence represents the progressive erosional development of a rocky coastal headland?

options.B: Wave-cut platform, delta, floodplain and levee

questions.explanation: Wave action enlarges weaknesses in a headland into caves, which may develop into arches. Collapse of the arch roof leaves a stack, which may eventually be reduced to a stump.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which process is primarily responsible for the formation of a wave-cut notch at the base of a sea cliff?
questions.explanation: Hydraulic action and abrasion by waves erode a recess at the foot of a sea cliff. This wave-cut notch undercuts the cliff and encourages collapse.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which statement best describes the formation of a tombolo?

options.A: A ridge of sediment connecting an island to the mainland or another island
options.B: A deep valley carved by a glacier and flooded by seawater
options.C: A narrow ridge attached to the mainland at only one end
options.D: A rocky platform formed by retreating sea cliffs

questions.explanation: A tombolo is a depositional ridge or bar that connects an island to the mainland or to another island.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which sequence best explains the development of an underground drainage system in limestone terrain?

options.A: Wind abrasion, dune migration and surface deposition
options.B: Carbon dioxide absorption by rainwater, weak carbonic acid formation, dissolution along joints and enlargement of underground conduits
options.C: Wave erosion, headland collapse and stack formation
options.D: Glacial plucking, moraine deposition and meltwater freezing

questions.explanation: Rainwater absorbs carbon dioxide and forms weak carbonic acid. It percolates through joints and bedding planes, dissolves limestone and enlarges openings into conduits and caves.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Coastal landforms are primarily shaped by which combination of geomorphic agents and processes?

options.A: Waves, tides, currents, erosion and deposition
options.B: Glaciers, volcanic eruptions and earthquakes only
options.C: Wind abrasion and groundwater dissolution only
options.D: River downcutting and glacial plucking only

questions.explanation: Coastal landforms are shaped by waves, tides, currents, coastal erosion, sediment transport and deposition.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which statement about coastal landforms is correct?

options.C: Coastal landforms may be either erosional or depositional
options.D: Coastal landforms are formed exclusively by groundwater

questions.explanation: Coastal processes produce erosional features such as cliffs and caves as well as depositional features such as beaches, spits and bars.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A sea cliff is best described as:

options.A: A steep rock face along the coast
options.B: A ridge of sand connecting an island to the mainland
options.C: A shallow coastal water body enclosed by a barrier

questions.explanation: A sea cliff is a steep coastal rock face formed mainly by wave erosion at its base, followed by undercutting and collapse.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The principal process responsible for the formation of a sea cliff is:

options.A: Wave erosion at the base followed by undercutting and collapse
options.D: Dissolution of limestone by carbonic acid

questions.explanation: Waves erode the foot of a coastal slope, undercutting it. The unsupported material eventually collapses, causing the cliff to retreat.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A wave-cut notch is formed at which part of a sea cliff?

options.C: At the centre of its inland slope

questions.explanation: A wave-cut notch is a recess eroded at the foot of a sea cliff by wave action, particularly hydraulic action and abrasion.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which processes are particularly responsible for forming a wave-cut notch?
questions.explanation: Wave action, particularly hydraulic action and abrasion, erodes a recess at the foot of a cliff and gradually undercuts it.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is the immediate geomorphic effect of a wave-cut notch on a sea cliff?

options.A: It undercuts the cliff and encourages collapse
options.B: It builds a sand dune at the cliff summit
options.C: It creates an underground limestone stream
options.D: It deposits a moraine at the cliff base

questions.explanation: A wave-cut notch weakens the base of a cliff through undercutting, making the overlying rock less stable and encouraging collapse.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A wave-cut platform is:

options.A: A gently seaward-sloping rocky surface left by retreating sea cliffs
options.B: A steep-sided valley formed by a glacier
options.C: A ridge of sand deposited across a bay
options.D: A depression formed by limestone dissolution

questions.explanation: A wave-cut platform is a gently seaward-sloping rocky surface exposed as a sea cliff retreats through repeated undercutting and collapse.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A wave-cut platform develops mainly because of:

options.A: Repeated undercutting and collapse of a sea cliff
options.C: Deposition of sediment by a glacier
options.D: Precipitation of calcium carbonate in caves

questions.explanation: Repeated wave erosion undercuts the cliff. As the cliff collapses and retreats, a gently sloping rocky platform is left behind.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which sequence best explains the development of a wave-cut platform?

options.A: Wave erosion at cliff base → notch formation → undercutting → collapse and cliff retreat → platform exposure
options.B: Wind deposition → dune formation → glacier movement → platform formation
options.C: Limestone dissolution → stalactite formation → cliff collapse → platform formation
options.D: River deposition → delta formation → sea cave formation → platform formation

questions.explanation: Wave erosion creates a notch at the cliff foot. Continued undercutting causes collapse and retreat, leaving a rocky platform.
questions.source: PDF: Sea Cliffs, Wave-Cut Notches and Wave-Cut Platforms

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Sea caves commonly develop where waves attack:

options.A: Joints, faults and other weaknesses in a headland
options.B: The centre of a sand dune
options.C: The surface of a glacial moraine
options.D: The floor of a limestone plateau far inland

questions.explanation: Waves exploit joints, faults and other weaknesses in coastal headlands. Hydraulic action and abrasion enlarge these openings into caves.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which processes enlarge weaknesses in a coastal headland to form a sea cave?
questions.explanation: Hydraulic action and abrasion by waves enlarge cracks, joints and faults in a headland, eventually producing sea caves.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A sea arch is formed when:

options.A: A sea cave is enlarged through a headland until it opens on the other side
options.B: A sand ridge connects an island to the mainland
options.C: A glacier deposits sediment across a valley
options.D: A river cuts off a meander loop

questions.explanation: Continued wave erosion enlarges a cave through a headland until it cuts through to the other side, creating a sea arch.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which coastal erosional feature is produced when a cave cuts through a headland?
questions.explanation: A sea arch forms when wave erosion enlarges a cave until it passes through the headland.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A sea stack is formed mainly by:

options.A: Collapse of the roof of a sea arch
options.B: Deposition of sand across a bay
options.C: Accumulation of sediment by a glacier

questions.explanation: When the roof of a sea arch collapses, an isolated pillar of rock remains offshore or close to the coast. This feature is called a sea stack.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A sea stack is best described as:

options.A: An isolated pillar of rock near or offshore from a coast
options.B: A shallow water body enclosed by a spit
options.C: A ridge of sand connecting an island to the mainland
options.D: A gently sloping rocky surface at the foot of a cliff

questions.explanation: A sea stack is an isolated rock pillar left after the collapse of a sea arch.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A stump is:

options.A: A low remnant of a sea stack after further erosion
options.C: A ridge of sand extending into an estuary

questions.explanation: A stump is a low remnant of a stack left after continued wave erosion and collapse. It may be visible mainly at low tide.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which is the correct order in the development of common coastal erosional features?
questions.explanation: Waves enlarge a weakness into a cave. Continued erosion may form an arch; its roof collapses to leave a stack, which is further reduced to a stump.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider the following statements about the cave–arch–stack–stump sequence: 1. A cave develops when waves exploit weaknesses in a headland. 2. An arch forms when a cave cuts through the headland. 3. A stack may remain after the arch roof collapses. 4. Continued erosion may reduce a stack to a stump. Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: All four statements describe the successive stages of coastal erosion in a headland.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an erosional coastal landform?
questions.explanation: A beach is a depositional feature formed by the accumulation of sand, shingle, pebbles or other sediment along the shore. Caves, arches and stacks are erosional features.
questions.source: PDF: Coastal Erosional and Depositional Landforms

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A beach is primarily formed by:

options.A: Accumulation of sediment along the shore

questions.explanation: A beach is a depositional landform consisting of accumulated sand, shingle, pebbles or other sediment along the shore.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which agents help shape beaches?

options.D: Wind abrasion and river downcutting only

questions.explanation: Beaches are accumulations of coastal sediment shaped by waves, tides and currents.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following materials may form a beach?
questions.explanation: Beaches may consist of sand, shingle, pebbles or other sediment accumulated along the shore.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A spit is a narrow ridge of sand or shingle that is generally:

options.A: Attached to the mainland at one end and extends into water

questions.explanation: A spit is a narrow depositional ridge attached to the mainland at one end and extending into a bay or estuary.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which process commonly forms a coastal spit?
questions.explanation: Longshore drift transports sediment along the coast and deposits it to form a narrow ridge attached to land at one end.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A spit commonly extends into which of the following?
questions.explanation: A spit is a narrow ridge of sediment extending from the mainland into a bay or estuary.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A coastal bar is:

options.A: A ridge of sand or shingle deposited across a bay or inlet
options.C: A long, streamlined ridge carved by wind
options.D: A deep valley carved by a glacier

questions.explanation: A bar is a ridge of sand or shingle deposited across a bay or inlet. It may connect headlands and partly or completely enclose a water body.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A coastal bar may:

options.A: Connect headlands and partly or completely enclose a water body

questions.explanation: A bar may extend across a bay or inlet, connect its sides and partly or completely enclose water behind it.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A tombolo is a depositional feature that connects:

options.A: An island to the mainland or to another island
options.D: A desert dune to a mountain

questions.explanation: A tombolo is a ridge or bar of deposited sediment connecting an island to the mainland or to another island.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is the defining characteristic of a tombolo?

options.A: It connects an island with the mainland or another island
options.B: It is a cave formed in a coastal headland
options.C: It is a ridge of glacial till
options.D: It is a wind-eroded rock pillar

questions.explanation: A tombolo is a depositional ridge or bar that creates a sediment connection between an island and the mainland or another island.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A lagoon is best described as:

options.A: A shallow water body separated from the open sea by a coastal barrier
options.B: A deep valley carved by a glacier
options.C: A steep rock face eroded by waves

questions.explanation: A lagoon is a shallow body of water separated from the open sea by a spit, bar, barrier island or reef, often with a restricted connection to the sea.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which coastal depositional features may separate a lagoon from the open sea?

options.A: Spit, bar, barrier island or reef
options.B: Sea cliff, cave, arch or stack

questions.explanation: A lagoon may be separated from the open sea by a spit, bar, barrier island or reef.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: How can a lagoon develop behind a coastal bar or spit?

options.A: Sediment deposition partly or completely encloses shallow coastal water
options.B: Glacial erosion deepens a river valley
options.C: Wind abrasion removes the upper part of a rock
options.D: Groundwater dissolves an underground limestone passage

questions.explanation: Longshore drift and wave action deposit sediment across a bay or along the coast. The deposit partly or completely encloses shallow coastal water, forming a lagoon.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which statement correctly differentiates a spit from a bar?

options.A: A spit is attached at one end, whereas a bar extends across a bay or inlet
options.B: A spit connects an island to the mainland, whereas a bar is always a sea cliff
options.C: A spit is erosional, whereas a bar is formed by glacial plucking

questions.explanation: A spit projects into water while remaining attached to land at one end. A bar extends across a bay or inlet and may join two sides, enclosing a lagoon.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following coastal landform and description pairs is INCORRECT?

options.A: Spit — attached to land at one end
options.B: Bar — ridge deposited across a bay or inlet
options.C: Tombolo — connects an island to the mainland or another island
options.D: Lagoon — isolated pillar left after a sea arch collapses

questions.explanation: A lagoon is a shallow coastal water body separated from the open sea by a barrier. An isolated pillar left after the collapse of a sea arch is a sea stack.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Longshore drift is important in the formation of which coastal landform?
questions.explanation: Longshore drift transports sediment along the coast and commonly contributes to the formation of spits.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which group consists entirely of coastal depositional landforms?

options.A: Beaches, spits, bars, tombolos and lagoons
options.B: Cliffs, caves, arches, stacks and wave-cut platforms
options.C: Caves, beaches, cliffs, arches and stacks
options.D: Wave-cut notches, bars, cliffs, caves and stumps

questions.explanation: Beaches, spits, bars, tombolos and lagoons are coastal depositional features. Cliffs, caves, arches, stacks and wave-cut platforms are erosional features.
questions.source: PDF: Coastal Erosional and Depositional Landforms

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which group consists entirely of coastal erosional landforms?

options.A: Sea cliffs, caves, arches, stacks and wave-cut platforms
options.B: Beaches, spits, bars, tombolos and lagoons
options.C: Beaches, sea caves, bars, cliffs and lagoons
options.D: Tombolos, stacks, spits, beaches and wave-cut platforms

questions.explanation: Sea cliffs, caves, arches, stacks and wave-cut platforms are identified as coastal erosional features in the study material.
questions.source: PDF: Coastal Erosional and Depositional Landforms

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which Indian coastal water body is identified in the study material as a major brackish coastal lagoon?
questions.explanation: Chilika Lake in Odisha is a major brackish coastal lagoon separated from the Bay of Bengal by a barrier or spit system.
questions.source: PDF: Indian Examples of Coastal Landforms

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Chilika Lake is located in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Chilika Lake is located in Odisha and is a major brackish coastal lagoon.
questions.source: PDF: Indian Examples of Coastal Landforms

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Chilika Lake is separated from the Bay of Bengal by:
questions.explanation: The PDF describes Chilika as a brackish coastal lagoon separated from the Bay of Bengal by a barrier or spit system.
questions.source: PDF: Indian Examples of Coastal Landforms

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Marina Beach, mentioned as a familiar coastal example in the study material, is associated with:
questions.explanation: Marina Beach is in Chennai, Tamil Nadu. The PDF identifies it as a familiar example of a coastal beach.
questions.source: PDF: Indian Examples of Coastal Landforms

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which Indian coastal region is mentioned alongside Marina Beach as an area where familiar coastal landforms occur?
questions.explanation: The study material mentions the Kerala coast as an area where beaches, spits, bars and lagoons occur.
questions.source: PDF: Indian Examples of Coastal Landforms

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which statement about Indian coastal landforms is supported by the study material?

options.A: Beaches, spits, bars and lagoons occur along both the eastern and western coasts
options.B: Coastal depositional features occur only along the eastern coast
options.D: All Indian coastal features are formed exclusively by glacial erosion

questions.explanation: The PDF notes that beaches, spits, bars and lagoons occur along both the eastern and western coasts of India. Individual features can vary over time.
questions.source: PDF: Indian Examples of Coastal Landforms

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider the following pairs: 1. Sea cliff — wave erosion; 2. Beach — sediment accumulation; 3. Spit — longshore drift; 4. Tombolo — island-mainland connection. Which pairs are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: All four pairs are correctly matched. Cliffs are formed by wave erosion, beaches by sediment accumulation, spits commonly by longshore drift, and tombolos connect islands to land.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?

options.A: A sea arch may form when a cave cuts through a headland
options.B: A sea stack may remain after an arch roof collapses
options.C: A spit is attached to the mainland at one end
options.D: A tombolo is a low remnant of a sea stack

questions.explanation: A tombolo is a depositional ridge connecting an island to the mainland or another island. A low remnant of a sea stack is called a stump.
questions.source: PDF: Coastal Erosional and Depositional Landforms

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which pair correctly distinguishes two coastal features?

options.A: Wave-cut platform — rocky surface left by cliff retreat; beach — accumulation of coastal sediment
options.B: Wave-cut platform — sand ridge across a bay; beach — isolated rock pillar
options.C: Wave-cut platform — island-mainland connection; beach — underground cave
options.D: Wave-cut platform — lagoon; beach — sea arch

questions.explanation: A wave-cut platform is an erosional rocky surface exposed by cliff retreat, whereas a beach is a depositional accumulation of coastal sediment.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A coastal ridge of sediment extends from the mainland into an estuary but remains attached to land at one end. Which landform is described?
questions.explanation: A spit is a narrow ridge of sand or shingle attached to the mainland at one end and extending into a bay or estuary.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A ridge of deposited sand connects an offshore island to the mainland. Which feature has developed?
questions.explanation: A tombolo is a depositional ridge or bar that connects an island to the mainland or to another island.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider the following coastal features: 1. Sea cave; 2. Sea arch; 3. Sea stack; 4. Beach; 5. Spit; 6. Tombolo. Which of these are depositional landforms?
questions.explanation: Beaches, spits and tombolos are depositional coastal features. Sea caves, arches and stacks are formed through wave erosion.
questions.source: PDF: Coastal Erosional and Depositional Landforms

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Karst topography is primarily associated with the action of:
questions.explanation: Karst topography develops mainly through the dissolving action of groundwater on soluble rocks, especially limestone.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which rock is most commonly associated with the development of karst landscapes?
questions.explanation: Limestone is readily dissolved by slightly acidic groundwater and is therefore the most characteristic rock associated with karst landscapes.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following groups consists entirely of rocks that can develop karst features through dissolution?
questions.explanation: Limestone, dolomite and gypsum are soluble rocks that can develop dissolution landforms under suitable conditions.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The chemical process mainly responsible for dissolving limestone in karst regions is:
questions.explanation: Carbonation occurs when carbon dioxide combines with water to form weak carbonic acid, which reacts with and dissolves limestone.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Carbonic acid in rainwater is mainly formed when rainwater absorbs:
questions.explanation: Rainwater absorbs carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and soil, forming weak carbonic acid that can dissolve carbonate rocks.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which chemical reaction best represents the dissolution of limestone by carbonic acid?

options.A: Calcium carbonate reacts with carbonic acid to form soluble calcium bicarbonate
options.B: Calcium carbonate reacts with oxygen to form granite
options.C: Limestone reacts with nitrogen to form gypsum
options.D: Calcium carbonate reacts with sand to form quartz

questions.explanation: Carbonic acid reacts with calcium carbonate in limestone to produce soluble calcium bicarbonate, which can be carried away by groundwater.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which geological structures commonly help groundwater enter and move through limestone?
questions.explanation: Joints and bedding planes provide pathways through which water can penetrate limestone and enlarge openings through dissolution.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A doline is another name for which karst landform?
questions.explanation: A doline is a closed depression in a karst landscape, commonly formed by the dissolution or collapse of soluble rock.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which process can directly produce a sinkhole in a limestone region?

options.B: Dissolution or collapse of underground limestone

questions.explanation: Sinkholes may develop when limestone is dissolved underground or when the roof of an underground cavity collapses.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A swallow hole in a karst region is a feature through which:

options.C: Sea waves enter a coastal cave

questions.explanation: A swallow hole is an opening through which surface water, often a stream, disappears into an underground drainage system.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which drainage characteristic is especially common in well-developed karst terrain?

options.A: A dense network of permanent surface rivers everywhere
options.B: Underground drainage through openings and caves

questions.explanation: Water commonly enters fissures, sinkholes and underground passages in karst terrain, resulting in extensive underground drainage.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A karst window is generally formed when:

options.A: An underground stream or cave becomes exposed at the surface
options.B: A glacier deposits a terminal moraine
options.C: A river cuts through a meander neck
options.D: Wind removes the top layer of sand

questions.explanation: A karst window is an opening that exposes part of an underground drainage system or cave passage at the surface.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Limestone caves are primarily formed through:
questions.explanation: Groundwater containing weak carbonic acid dissolves limestone along joints and bedding planes, gradually enlarging openings into caves.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The development of a limestone cave is most directly associated with:

options.A: The gradual enlargement of rock openings by dissolution
options.C: The deposition of river gravel at a mountain front

questions.explanation: Groundwater enlarges pre-existing joints and fissures in soluble limestone through chemical dissolution, eventually creating cave passages.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Stalactites are cave formations that hang from the:
questions.explanation: Stalactites are mineral deposits that grow downwards from the ceilings of caves.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Stalagmites develop on the:
questions.explanation: Stalagmites grow upwards from the cave floor as mineral-rich water deposits calcite after dripping from the ceiling.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes stalactites from stalagmites?

options.A: Stalactites grow from the floor and stalagmites from the ceiling
options.C: Stalactites hang from ceilings while stalagmites rise from floors
options.D: Stalactites are formed by wind and stalagmites by glaciers

questions.explanation: Stalactites hang down from cave ceilings, whereas stalagmites build upwards from cave floors.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The mineral commonly deposited to form stalactites and stalagmites in limestone caves is:
questions.explanation: Calcite, a form of calcium carbonate, is commonly precipitated from mineral-rich water to form cave deposits.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Stalactites and stalagmites are mainly formed when groundwater containing dissolved calcium bicarbonate:

options.A: Loses carbon dioxide and deposits calcium carbonate
options.B: Absorbs more sand and forms sandstone

questions.explanation: When mineral-rich water loses carbon dioxide, and sometimes through evaporation, calcium carbonate becomes less soluble and is deposited as calcite.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a depositional feature inside a limestone cave?
questions.explanation: Stalactites are depositional cave features formed by the precipitation of calcium carbonate from mineral-rich water.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A limestone cave passage is generally classified as which type of landform?
questions.explanation: Limestone cave passages are commonly enlarged by the dissolution of soluble rock by groundwater.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which sequence correctly represents the major processes involved in the formation of limestone caves and their mineral deposits?

options.A: Dissolution of limestone, movement of mineral-rich water, and precipitation of calcite
options.B: Glacial plucking, wind abrasion, and deposition of sand
options.C: River meandering, delta formation, and marine erosion
options.D: Volcanic eruption, lava cooling, and soil formation

questions.explanation: Groundwater first dissolves limestone and carries dissolved minerals. When conditions change inside the cave, calcite can precipitate and form stalactites and stalagmites.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic surface feature of karst topography?
questions.explanation: A doline or sinkhole is a characteristic closed depression formed in soluble rock landscapes.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT primarily a karst landform?
questions.explanation: A moraine is deposited by a glacier, whereas sinkholes, limestone caves and stalactites are associated with karst processes.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which condition most directly favours the development of karst topography?

options.A: Presence of soluble rocks with openings that allow water to penetrate
options.B: Presence of permanently frozen ground only

questions.explanation: Karst development is favoured where soluble rocks such as limestone are exposed to water that can enter joints and bedding planes and dissolve the rock.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Why is groundwater in a limestone region often capable of enlarging underground cavities?

options.A: It contains weak carbonic acid that dissolves calcium carbonate

questions.explanation: Groundwater containing dissolved carbon dioxide forms weak carbonic acid, which reacts with calcium carbonate and gradually enlarges fissures and cavities.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which pair consists of two karst features associated mainly with the removal or dissolution of limestone?
questions.explanation: Sinkholes and limestone caves are associated with dissolution or collapse in soluble rock. Stalactites and stalagmites are mineral deposits.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which pair consists entirely of depositional features found inside limestone caves?
questions.explanation: Stalactites and stalagmites form through the deposition of calcite from mineral-rich water inside caves.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is the likely result when calcium-rich water repeatedly drips from a limestone cave ceiling onto the floor?

options.A: A stalactite may grow from the ceiling and a stalagmite from the floor
options.B: A barchan dune forms inside the cave
options.D: A river delta forms beneath the cave roof

questions.explanation: Mineral-rich droplets can deposit calcite on the ceiling and floor, producing stalactites above and stalagmites below.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: When a stalactite and a stalagmite join together, they may form a:
questions.explanation: A stalactite growing downward and a stalagmite growing upward can eventually meet to form a cave column or pillar.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which Indian region is particularly well known for limestone caves and karst features?

options.A: Khasi and Jaintia Hills of Meghalaya
options.D: Malwa Plateau of Madhya Pradesh only

questions.explanation: The Khasi and Jaintia Hills of Meghalaya are well known for extensive limestone cave systems and associated karst features.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The limestone caves of Meghalaya are mainly associated with which geological process?
questions.explanation: Groundwater containing carbonic acid dissolves limestone, producing caves and other karst features in Meghalaya.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following Indian states is especially associated with extensive limestone caves in the Khasi and Jaintia Hills?
questions.explanation: The Khasi and Jaintia Hills are located in Meghalaya and contain well-known limestone cave systems.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which statement about karst landscapes is correct?

options.A: They develop only in regions covered by glaciers
options.B: They are associated with soluble rocks and groundwater dissolution
options.C: They are formed exclusively by wind deposition
options.D: They are found only along sea coasts

questions.explanation: Karst landscapes develop where soluble rocks are dissolved by water, commonly producing sinkholes, caves and underground drainage.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the relationship between sinkholes and underground drainage?

options.A: Sinkholes can provide entry points for surface water into underground drainage systems
options.B: Sinkholes prevent all water from entering limestone
options.C: Sinkholes are formed only by glaciers
options.D: Sinkholes are depositional features formed by sea waves

questions.explanation: Sinkholes may allow surface water to enter underground passages, contributing to the development of underground drainage in karst regions.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a swallow hole from a stalactite?

options.A: A swallow hole is an opening through which water enters underground, while a stalactite is a mineral deposit hanging from a cave ceiling
options.C: A swallow hole is a cave deposit, while a stalactite is a surface depression
options.D: Both are formed by wind abrasion

questions.explanation: A swallow hole is associated with the movement of surface water underground, whereas a stalactite is formed by calcite deposition inside a cave.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches the karst feature with its principal process?
questions.explanation: A doline is a closed depression produced by dissolution or collapse in soluble rock. The other process-feature combinations are incorrect.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a typical example of underground drainage in a karst region?

options.A: A surface stream disappearing into a swallow hole
options.B: A river forming a natural levee
options.D: A coastal current forming a spit

questions.explanation: Surface streams can disappear into swallow holes and continue through underground passages in karst terrain.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a groundwater-related erosional landform?

options.D: Cave column formed by calcite deposition

questions.explanation: Limestone caves are enlarged by groundwater dissolution, while stalactites, stalagmites and columns are depositional cave formations.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a groundwater-related depositional landform?
questions.explanation: Stalagmites form through the deposition of calcite on cave floors from dripping mineral-rich water.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which statement about calcium bicarbonate in karst processes is correct?

options.A: It is a soluble product formed when carbonic acid reacts with limestone
options.B: It is an insoluble wind-blown sediment
options.C: It is a type of glacial ice
options.D: It is the main material forming volcanic cones

questions.explanation: Carbonic acid reacts with calcium carbonate in limestone to form soluble calcium bicarbonate, which can be transported by groundwater.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which condition can encourage calcium carbonate deposition inside a limestone cave?

options.A: Loss of carbon dioxide from mineral-rich water
options.B: Continuous addition of carbon dioxide under all conditions
options.C: Glacial plucking of the cave floor

questions.explanation: When mineral-rich water loses carbon dioxide, calcium carbonate can precipitate and accumulate as calcite deposits.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following statements about dolines is correct?

options.A: They are closed depressions characteristic of karst landscapes
options.B: They are long ridges deposited by glaciers

questions.explanation: Dolines, also known as sinkholes, are closed depressions formed in soluble rocks through dissolution or collapse.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider the following statements about karst topography: 1. It commonly develops in limestone. 2. Groundwater dissolution is an important process. 3. Underground drainage may occur. Which of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: All three statements are correct. Soluble limestone, groundwater dissolution and underground drainage are fundamental characteristics of karst terrain.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider the following pairs: 1. Stalactite - cave ceiling. 2. Stalagmite - cave floor. 3. Doline - surface depression. Which pairs are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: All three pairs are correctly matched: stalactites hang from cave ceilings, stalagmites rise from floors, and dolines are closed surface depressions.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which sequence correctly classifies the following features according to their dominant origin: sinkhole, stalactite and limestone cave?

options.C: Wind erosion, river deposition, marine erosion
options.D: Glacial deposition, wind deposition, marine deposition

questions.explanation: Sinkholes form through dissolution or collapse, stalactites form by mineral deposition, and limestone caves are enlarged through dissolution.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following Indian regions is also associated with limestone cave formations, apart from Meghalaya?

options.A: Parts of Andhra Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh

questions.explanation: Limestone cave formations are also found in parts of Andhra Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, as noted in the source material.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following correctly identifies the dominant geomorphic agent and its associated landforms?

options.A: Groundwater - sinkholes, limestone caves and cave deposits
options.C: Glaciers - dolines, swallow holes and spits
options.D: Sea waves - drumlins, eskers and sinkholes

questions.explanation: Groundwater produces karst features through dissolution and deposition, including sinkholes, limestone caves, stalactites and stalagmites.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following statements about stalactites and stalagmites is INCORRECT?

options.B: Stalagmites grow upwards from cave floors
options.C: Both can form through calcite deposition
options.D: Both are produced primarily by glacial abrasion

questions.explanation: Stalactites and stalagmites are formed by calcite deposition from mineral-rich water, not by glacial abrasion.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A region has limestone bedrock, numerous closed depressions, underground streams and caves containing calcite deposits. Which geomorphic environment does this description best represent?
questions.explanation: Limestone bedrock, dolines or sinkholes, underground drainage and calcite cave deposits are characteristic features of a karst landscape.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is correctly matched with its principal geomorphic agent?
questions.explanation: Barchans are crescent-shaped sand dunes formed by wind deposition. V-shaped valleys are commonly formed by rivers, moraines by glaciers, and stalactites by groundwater deposition.
questions.source: PDF - Comparative study of landforms by different agents

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which pair consists entirely of river erosional landforms?
questions.explanation: V-shaped valleys and gorges are produced mainly by river erosion. Deltas, floodplains, natural levees, alluvial fans and point bars are depositional features. An ox-bow lake develops through meander cut-off.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following pairs consists entirely of glacial erosional landforms?
questions.explanation: Cirques and arêtes are formed by glacial erosion. Drumlins, eskers and moraines are associated with glacial deposition.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a wind-erosional landform?
questions.explanation: Yardangs are elongated features carved by wind erosion and abrasion. Loess and dunes are depositional landforms.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a coastal depositional landform?
questions.explanation: A spit is formed by the deposition of sediment transported along the coast by longshore drift. Sea cliffs, wave-cut platforms and sea caves are erosional features.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is correctly classified as a groundwater depositional feature?
questions.explanation: A stalagmite forms when calcite is deposited on a cave floor. Dolines, swallow holes and limestone caves are primarily associated with dissolution or underground drainage.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A V-shaped valley is most characteristically associated with:
questions.explanation: A river cuts vertically into its bed, particularly in its upper course, producing a narrow V-shaped valley.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A broad U-shaped valley is most commonly produced by:
questions.explanation: A glacier erodes and widens a pre-existing valley, producing a broad trough with steep sides and a relatively flat floor.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a V-shaped valley from a U-shaped valley?

options.A: V-shaped valleys are generally river-formed, while U-shaped valleys are generally glacier-formed
options.B: Both are exclusively formed by wind deposition
options.C: V-shaped valleys are coastal depositional features, while U-shaped valleys are karst features
options.D: Both are formed only by groundwater dissolution

questions.explanation: River erosion commonly creates V-shaped valleys, whereas glacial erosion produces broad U-shaped valleys or glacial troughs.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which pair is correctly matched with the type of sediment it commonly contains?

options.B: Esker - Unsorted material deposited directly by ice
options.C: Loess - Coarse boulders deposited by glaciers
options.D: Barchan - Fine silt deposited by rivers

questions.explanation: Glacial till is generally unsorted material deposited directly by ice. Eskers are commonly made of stratified sand and gravel deposited by meltwater streams.
questions.source: PDF - Glacial and aeolian depositional landforms

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which glacial depositional feature is commonly composed of stratified sand and gravel laid down by meltwater streams?
questions.explanation: Eskers are winding ridges formed from sand and gravel deposited by streams flowing within or beneath glaciers.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which feature is formed by the deposition of wind-blown fine silt over extensive areas?
questions.explanation: Loess is a blanket-like deposit of fine, wind-blown silt that can cover extensive areas.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes loess from sand dunes?

options.A: Loess consists mainly of fine wind-blown silt, whereas dunes consist mainly of accumulated sand
options.B: Loess is deposited by glaciers, whereas dunes are deposited by rivers
options.C: Loess is a marine erosional feature, whereas dunes are karst features
options.D: Both are formed exclusively by groundwater

questions.explanation: Both are aeolian depositional features, but loess consists mainly of fine silt while dunes are accumulations of sand.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which type of dune is characteristically crescent-shaped and has horns pointing in the direction of the prevailing wind?
questions.explanation: Barchan dunes are crescent-shaped dunes whose horns point downwind. They commonly form where sand is limited and wind direction is relatively consistent.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which dune type commonly has arms pointing upwind and is often associated with vegetation?
questions.explanation: Parabolic dunes commonly have U-shaped forms with arms pointing upwind, often stabilised by vegetation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which statement about barchan and parabolic dunes is correct?

options.B: Barchan horns point downwind, while parabolic dune arms point upwind
options.C: Barchans are formed by glaciers, while parabolic dunes are formed by sea waves
options.D: Both are erosional features carved into solid rock

questions.explanation: The orientation of their horns or arms is an important distinction: barchan horns point downwind, whereas parabolic dune arms point upwind.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which landform is produced when a river cuts down into its bed and creates a deep, narrow valley with steep sides?
questions.explanation: A gorge is a deep, narrow valley with steep sides, commonly formed by prolonged river downcutting.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A waterfall may retreat upstream over time mainly because of:

options.A: Undercutting and collapse of rock near its base
options.B: Deposition of loess on the valley floor
options.D: Longshore drift along the river bank

questions.explanation: Waterfall erosion can undercut the rock at the base, forming a plunge pool and causing overhanging rock to collapse. Repeated collapse leads to upstream retreat.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: In a meandering river, erosion is generally strongest on the:
questions.explanation: The faster current along the outer bank causes erosion and forms a cut bank. Deposition commonly occurs along the inner bank, producing a point bar.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A point bar is most commonly formed by:

options.A: Deposition along the inner bend of a meander
options.B: Glacial erosion along a mountain ridge
options.C: Wind abrasion of a rock surface

questions.explanation: Sediment is deposited on the inner side of a meander where water velocity is relatively lower, forming a point bar.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: An ox-bow lake is formed when:

options.A: A meander loop is cut off from the main river channel
options.B: A glacier deposits a ridge of till
options.D: Wind deposits sand in a crescent shape

questions.explanation: Erosion and deposition can narrow a meander neck until the river cuts through it, leaving the former loop isolated as an ox-bow lake.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which river depositional feature develops when a river leaves a mountainous valley and spreads sediment over a flatter area?
questions.explanation: An alluvial fan commonly forms where a stream emerges from a steep mountain valley onto a flatter plain, loses velocity and deposits sediment.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A delta is generally formed at the:
questions.explanation: A delta forms where a river enters a standing body of water and deposits sediment, often dividing into distributary channels.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes an alluvial fan from a delta?

options.A: An alluvial fan commonly forms where a stream emerges from a mountain valley, while a delta forms at a river mouth
options.B: Both form only through glacial deposition
options.C: A delta forms at a mountain front, while an alluvial fan forms only in the sea
options.D: An alluvial fan is an erosional feature, while a delta is a volcanic feature

questions.explanation: An alluvial fan commonly develops at the transition from a steep valley to a flatter plain, whereas a delta develops at a river mouth through sediment deposition.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which glacial landform is a bowl-shaped hollow at the head of a mountain valley?
questions.explanation: A cirque, also known as a corrie or cwm, is a bowl-shaped hollow formed by glacial erosion near the head of a mountain valley.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A tarn is commonly found:

options.B: At the mouth of a delta
options.C: On the crest of a barchan

questions.explanation: A tarn is a small lake that occupies a cirque or corrie after glacial retreat.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: An arête is best described as:

options.A: A sharp ridge formed between adjacent glacial valleys or cirques
options.C: A depositional ridge formed by longshore drift
options.D: A depression formed by groundwater dissolution

questions.explanation: An arête is a narrow, sharp-edged ridge produced when glaciers erode adjacent sides of a mountain.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A pyramidal mountain peak formed by glacial erosion from several directions is known as a:
questions.explanation: A horn is a sharp pyramidal peak formed when several cirques erode a mountain from different sides.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A fjord is generally a:
questions.explanation: A fjord is a long, narrow, deep inlet formed when a glacially carved valley is submerged by the sea.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which glacial depositional feature is a ridge of debris marking the farthest advance of a glacier?
questions.explanation: A terminal or end moraine marks the maximum extent reached by a glacier and consists of material deposited at its snout.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A medial moraine is generally formed by:

options.A: The joining of lateral moraines where two glaciers meet
options.B: The deposition of sand by coastal waves
options.C: The collapse of a limestone cave
options.D: The erosion of a river meander

questions.explanation: When two valley glaciers join, their adjacent lateral moraines may combine to form a medial moraine running along the centre of the combined glacier.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A drumlin is best described as a:
questions.explanation: Drumlins are elongated, streamlined hills commonly composed of glacial till and shaped beneath moving ice.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which process involves the removal of rock fragments by a moving glacier?
questions.explanation: Plucking occurs when glacier ice freezes onto fractured rock and removes pieces as the glacier moves.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The wearing away of bedrock by rock fragments carried within moving glacier ice is known as:
questions.explanation: Glacial abrasion occurs when debris embedded in moving ice scrapes and grinds the underlying bedrock.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which pair correctly identifies the two important processes of wind erosion?
questions.explanation: Wind erodes by deflation, the removal of loose particles, and abrasion, the wearing away of surfaces by wind-driven particles.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A mushroom rock is commonly formed because:

options.A: Wind-driven sand abrades the lower part of a rock more strongly
options.B: A glacier deposits a ridge on the rock
options.C: Groundwater deposits calcite on the rock
options.D: River water deposits a delta around the rock

questions.explanation: Wind-driven sand commonly abrades the lower portion of exposed rocks more strongly, producing a narrow base and wider upper part.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes a yardang?

options.A: An elongated ridge carved by wind erosion
options.B: A crescent-shaped dune deposited by a river

questions.explanation: Yardangs are elongated ridges formed by wind erosion, commonly aligned with the prevailing wind direction.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Zeugen are erosional landforms associated with wind action. Loess is wind-deposited silt, moraines are glacial deposits, and tombolos are coastal depositional features.
questions.source: PDF - Aeolian, glacial and coastal landforms

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which coastal landform is produced by wave erosion along a resistant headland?
questions.explanation: Waves exploit joints and weaknesses in a headland, enlarging openings into sea caves. Spits, tombolos and beaches are depositional features.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which sequence correctly represents the development of common erosional coastal landforms?

options.A: Sea cave, sea arch, sea stack and stump

questions.explanation: Wave erosion can enlarge a cave through a headland into an arch. Collapse of the arch leaves a stack, which may later be reduced to a stump.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Longshore drift is primarily responsible for:

options.B: Removing rock fragments from a glacier

questions.explanation: Longshore drift transports sediment along the coast through the combined action of waves approaching at an angle and the returning backwash.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A tombolo is a depositional feature that:

options.A: Connects an island to the mainland or another island
options.B: Forms a deep valley beneath a glacier
options.D: Forms through wind abrasion of a rock

questions.explanation: A tombolo is a ridge or bar of deposited sediment that connects an island to the mainland or to another island.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a spit from a bar?

options.A: A spit is attached to land at one end, while a bar may extend across a bay or inlet
options.B: A spit is formed by glaciers, while a bar is formed by groundwater
options.C: A spit is a rock ridge formed by wind erosion, while a bar is a river gorge
options.D: Both are erosional features formed by sea cliffs

questions.explanation: A spit is a narrow depositional ridge attached to the coast at one end. A bar is a depositional feature that may extend across a bay or inlet.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is an Indian example of a coastal lagoon?
questions.explanation: Chilika Lake in Odisha is a large brackish-water coastal lagoon separated from the Bay of Bengal by a barrier or spit system.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which chemical process is primarily responsible for the formation of limestone caves?
questions.explanation: Carbonation produces weak carbonic acid in water, which dissolves limestone and enlarges underground openings into caves.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which pair consists of two characteristic karst erosional or dissolution features?
questions.explanation: Dolines are closed depressions and swallow holes are openings through which surface water enters underground drainage. Both are associated with karst dissolution.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider the following pairs: 1. Cirque - Glacial erosion. 2. Drumlin - Glacial deposition. 3. Yardang - Wind erosion. 4. Loess - Wind deposition. Which pairs are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: All four pairs are correctly matched. Cirques are glacial erosional features, drumlins are glacial depositional features, yardangs are wind-erosional features, and loess is wind-deposited silt.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. A delta forms at a river mouth. 2. A spit is associated with longshore drift. 3. A sea stack develops through coastal erosion. Which of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: All three statements are correct. Deltas form through river sediment deposition at river mouths, spits through coastal sediment transport and deposition, and stacks through wave erosion and arch collapse.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which set contains only depositional landforms?

options.B: Gorge, cirque, yardang and sea cave
options.C: V-shaped valley, arête, sinkhole and sea cliff
options.D: Waterfall, horn, zeugen and wave-cut platform

questions.explanation: Deltas are river deposits, moraines are glacial deposits, loess is wind-blown silt, and spits are coastal deposits. The other options contain erosional features.
questions.source: PDF - Comparative study of landforms by different agents

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A landscape contains V-shaped valleys, U-shaped troughs, crescent-shaped dunes, sea arches and limestone caves. Which conclusion is most appropriate?

options.A: All features were formed by a single geomorphic agent
options.B: The landscape has been shaped by several geomorphic agents
options.D: The landscape has been shaped exclusively by endogenic forces

questions.explanation: The features indicate the action of several agents: rivers form V-shaped valleys, glaciers form U-shaped troughs, wind forms crescent-shaped dunes, waves form sea arches, and groundwater dissolves limestone to create caves.
questions.source: PDF - Introduction and comparative study of landforms by different agents
